articles.title: Super Sunday for India! Lakshya Sen ends year-long title drought as PV Sindhu completes Hylo Open double delight
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Indian badminton enjoyed a memorable Super Sunday at the Hylo Open 2026 as Lakshya Sen ended his year-long wait for a BWF World Tour title,
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Indian badminton enjoyed a memorable Super Sunday at the Hylo Open 2026 as Lakshya Sen ended his year-long wait for a BWF World Tour title, joining PV Sindhu in winning the men's and women's singles crowns at the Super 500 tournament in Saarbrücken, Germany.Lakshya produced a commanding performance to defeat Indonesia's fourth seed Jonatan Christie 21-17, 21-10 in the men's singles final, bringing an end to his title drought that had stretched back to the Australian Open in November 2025.Earlier, double Olympic medallist Sindhu had clinched the women's singles title with a dominant 21-12, 21-14 victory over Denmark's Line Højmark Kjærsfeldt. The two straight-game victories ensured India walked away with both singles trophies, capping a remarkable campaign at the USD 500,000 event.For Lakshya, the victory was particularly significant after a season disrupted by injuries and inconsistent performances. The 25-year-old had reached the All England Championships final earlier this year but had struggled to maintain that level in subsequent tournaments.Lakshya dominates Christie to end title droughtThe men's singles final initially developed into a closely fought contest, with both players engaging in fast-paced rallies and exchanging powerful smashes.Lakshya made an aggressive start to take an 8-4 lead, using sharp cross-court angles and attacking strokes to push Christie around the court. The Indonesian, however, responded with a five-point run to move ahead 9-8.The Indian recovered his composure and gradually regained control through solid defence, deceptive net play and well-directed smashes. He held his nerve in the closing exchanges to take the opening game 21-17.The second game was far more one-sided. Lakshya raised his intensity, capitalising on Christie's unforced errors while controlling the rallies with excellent movement and shot selection.The Indian repeatedly neutralised the Indonesian's attacking strokes and turned defence into counter-attacking opportunities. Christie struggled to find answers as Lakshya extended his advantage and eventually sealed the game 21-10 to secure the title.The victory also levelled Lakshya's career head-to-head record against Christie at 4-4.Sindhu leads India's double title celebrationSindhu had set the tone for India's title-winning Sunday by defeating Kjærsfeldt in the women's singles final.It was Sindhu's second title of the season after her Japan Open triumph in July. She had also finished runner-up at the French Open last week, making the Hylo Open victory another significant boost to her late-season campaign.The Indian's title run also earned her 9,200 ranking points, keeping her in contention for qualification for the season-ending BWF World Tour Finals.Lakshya had also spoken about rediscovering his rhythm after an injury-interrupted period following his semifinal victory."I've had a few niggles here and there, and I was out for some time. At certain tournaments, I wasn't really 100 per cent. But I'm happy with the way I've played here. It's a really good confidence booster because I haven't played this many matches in a row over the last couple of months," he had said."I'm really happy to reach another final. Since the All England Championships, I think this is the first time I've felt that I was playing really well again. I can feel myself getting back into rhythm and playing good badminton."With Sindhu and Lakshya both finishing on top of the podium, India secured a memorable double at the Hylo Open, with the two leading shuttlers delivering a timely boost ahead of the closing stretch of the badminton season.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'You are horrible': Rex Ryan rips into Ashton Jeanty after Raiders RB's Jets criticism
articles.summary: Ahead of Jets vs. Raiders on Sunday, New York's former head coach was not happy with Jeanty's choice of words.
articles.body:
Ahead of the Raiders ' matchup with the Jets this week, star running back Ashton Jeanty had some rather interesting words about the defense he would be facing.

Jeanty, who has managed just 3.1 yards per carry so far this season but been effective as a receiver, took a dig at the Jets' tackling ability before he lined up in the backfield against them on Sunday.

On ESPN, former Jets head coach Rex Ryan wasn't happy about Jeanty's comments, ripping into the former Heisman runner-up by calling him "the worst draft pick" among running backs in the last 20 years.

Here's what Ryan said about Jeanty's criticism of the Jets' defense.

Rex Ryan rips into Ashton Jeanty after Jets criticism

Before Sunday's game, Jeanty was talking about the Jets' defense earlier this week and what the Raiders will be able to do.

He noted there are "a couple of guys that don't really tackle" for New York, though he didn't want to say "names."

In response on ESPN, Ryan first broke down some strong tacklers on the Jets' defense, including Demario Davis, before ripping into Jeanty.

The former coach said that if he were still coaching, he would approach Jeanty and tell him, "We are not going to try to take you out of the game."

"Why? Because you are horrible. You're about the worst draft pick of the last 20 years, I think, as a running back," Ryan said. "You stink. You're averaging 3.1 yards per carry. ... It's on you, my friend."

Ryan has never been shy about his football thoughts — especially when it comes to his former Jets franchise.

Of course, it's likely an exaggeration to call Jeanty the worst running back draft pick of the last 20 years; he's been good for the Raiders, but not quite great. As a rookie, he finished with 975 rushing yards and 10 total touchdowns. So far in 2026, he's been extremely inefficient as a rusher, but effective as a receiver.

Jeanty has begun to cede backfield work to his backup, rookie Mike Washington Jr. If he can't perform against the Jets on Sunday, Ryan may just have more words for the Raiders' second-year back.

articles.body:
Juventus face Napoli in a match that could be crucial for Luciano Spalletti as he looks to save his job and avoid back-to-back league defeats. This is the team put out by the manager as he looks to get Juve back to winning ways.

This should be a match between two title challengers, but on paper it is a game between two top teams that have both struggled with inconsistency this season. Napoli are not the best travellers, but Juventus still need to raise their level if they are to secure a positive result.

Juventus have time to turn their season around, and this game could serve as a turning point. The team need to win and, at the very least, avoid another defeat in front of their own fans at the Allianz Stadium.

The players lack confidence, and fans will hope that the training retreat imposed by Spalletti will help them improve. The retreat is intended to bring the squad together and prepare them for a match that carries significant importance for the club.

If Juventus fail to get a result and Napoli leave Turin with all three points, it could create further problems for the club in their upcoming matches. Spalletti's position could come under even greater scrutiny, particularly if the team do not improve before the next international break.

Juventus need their players to compete at their best if they are to beat Napoli. The squad have the quality to get a result, but they must show greater belief and consistency than they have in recent weeks.

Spalletti knows what is at stake, and the outcome of this game could shape the direction of Juventus' season. A win would ease the pressure and provide a platform to build on, while another defeat could deepen the club's difficulties and raise further questions about the manager's future.

articles.title: Liverpool vs Arsenal: The tactics board - Kai Havertz proves the difference as Mikel Arteta wins the central duel
articles.summary: Arsenal secured a disciplined 1-0 victory at Anfield through a clinical Kai Havertz strike and a masterclass in defensive organisation. Mikel Arteta’s side s...
articles.body:
Arsenal secured a disciplined 1-0 victory at Anfield through a clinical Kai Havertz strike and a masterclass in defensive organisation. Mikel Arteta's side successfully nullified Liverpool's high-octane build-up, restricting the hosts to just four shots on target despite conceding the lion's share of possession.

This was a fixture defined by spatial control and the suppression of transition. Andoni Iraola's Liverpool entered the contest aiming to exploit the half-spaces and overwhelm Arsenal with a fluid 4-2-3-1 that often resembled a 3-2-5 in possession. By pushing Milos Kerkez high and asking Florian Wirtz to float between the lines, Iraola sought to pull Arsenal's defensive block out of shape, creating avenues for Alexander Isak to exploit the depth. The objective was clear: high-intensity pressing to force errors and rapid verticality to punish them.

Conversely, Arteta prioritised central compactness and structural discipline. Knowing the volatility of Anfield, Arsenal operated in a highly coordinated 4-2-3-1 that transitioned into a mid-block 4-4-2 when Liverpool's centre-backs had the ball. The strategy was not to dominate the ball - as evidenced by their 44% possession - but to control the zones where Liverpool are most dangerous. By deploying Declan Rice and Bruno Guimaraes as a double pivot, Arteta erected a barrier that effectively quarantined Liverpool's creative engines, allowing Havertz to act as the primary outlet in transition.

Iraola opted for a 4-2-3-1 formation that relied heavily on the technical proficiency of Alexis Mac Allister and the teenage Trey Nyoni in the pivot. The tactical blueprint was designed to invite Arsenal's press before bypassing it with diagonal balls to the flanks, particularly targeting the width provided by Bradley Barcola and Cody Gakpo. Liverpool's build-up pattern involved Virgil van Dijk acting as the primary distributor, looking to find Wirtz in the pockets. However, the pressing triggers - usually activated when the ball was played into Arsenal's full-backs - were frequently bypassed by David Raya's long distribution.

Defensively, Liverpool maintained a high line, with Ronald Araujo and van Dijk tasked with managing the space behind them. The plan was to squeeze the game into the middle third, but the lack of pressure on Rice in the 16th minute proved fatal. Despite Liverpool's 56% possession and 18 total shots, their inability to generate high-quality chances was a direct result of their predictable wide delivery. With 33 crosses attempted, Liverpool fell into the trap of playing around the Arsenal block rather than through it. The host's xG of 1.31 suggests they created moments of danger, but only registering four shot on target highlights a significant failure in the final third execution against a well-drilled low block.

Arteta's side mirrored the 4-2-3-1 formation but with vastly different functional roles. The key was the defensive screening provided by Rice and Guimaraes. Their primary instruction was to shadow Wirtz and prevent Mac Allister from dictate play. Arsenal's defensive shape was exemplary; they recorded 26 interceptions, illustrating their ability to read Liverpool's passing lanes. Gabriel and Riccardo Calafiori remained vertically compact, ensuring Isak had no room to turn or run into channels. This forced Liverpool wide, where Arsenal felt comfortable defending the box.

In possession, Arsenal were direct and purposeful. The winning goal in the 16th minute was a tactical archetype: Rice finding the space to provide the assist for Havertz, who exploited a momentary lapse in Liverpool's central marking. Havertz functioned as a 'false nine' who could drop deep to create a midfield overload or push onto the last man to stretch the defense. By utilising Noni Madueke and Christos Tzolis as hardworking wingers who tracked back diligently, Arteta ensured that Liverpool's full-backs, particularly Kerkez, were never allowed to create two-on-one situations. It was a performance of supreme tactical maturity, prioritising the scoreline over aesthetic dominance.

The decisive battle took place in the 'Zone 14' area - the space just outside the penalty box. Liverpool's system is designed to feed Wirtz in this area, but Arteta's decision to use a double pivot of Rice and Guimaraes effectively shuttered this corridor. The statistical evidence is stark: despite 18 shots, Liverpool only managed four efforts on target. This indicates that while Liverpool could reach the final third, they were forced into low-probability shots from distance or headers under extreme pressure.

Arteta won the tactical battle by identifying that Liverpool's greatest weakness under Iraola is their vulnerability to patient, vertical counters. By conceding possession, Arsenal drew Liverpool's mid-block forward, creating the very space Havertz needed for the opening goal. Once ahead, Arsenal's switch to a deeper block dared Liverpool to beat them in the air - a challenge Gabriel and Calafiori met with 17 clearances. Iraola's insistence on crossing (33 total) played directly into Arsenal's hands, representing a failure to adapt to the physical profile of the Gunners' backline.

Iraola recognized the stagnation of his attack relatively early. In the 59th minute, he replaced Nyoni with Dominik Szoboszlai, attempting to add more athleticism and direct running to the midfield. Further changes in the 67th and 81st minutes saw the introduction of Rio Ngumoha, Kostas Tsimikas, and Lewis Koumas. These substitutions shifted Liverpool toward a more aggressive, almost 4-2-4 shape in the closing stages. While this increased the volume of pressure, it did not improve the quality of chances, as Arsenal's structure remained unyielding.

Arteta's responses were purely reactive and aimed at preservation. The introduction of Myles Lewis-Skelly for Guimaraes in the 62nd minute fortified the left side, though the youngster's yellow card in the 72nd minute added tension. Arteta later moved to a five-man defense by bringing on Piero Hincapie for Havertz in the 84th minute, effectively killing the game. The substitution of Mikel Merino for Martin Oedegaard in the 88th minute further reinforced the central block. These tweaks ensured that despite Liverpool's late flurry of corners, David Raya was rarely forced into a difficult save, perfectly executing the game-state management Arteta demanded.

Ultimately, the match was decided by Arsenal's superior defensive floor and Liverpool's lack of a 'Plan B' when central avenues were blocked. Arteta's tactical gamble to cede the ball and rely on structural integrity paid dividends, as Liverpool's 18 shots yielded almost no genuine threat. The 16th-minute goal from Havertz allowed Arsenal to retreat into a shape that Liverpool simply could not dismantle. By forcing the hosts into wide areas and winning the aerial duel in the box, Arsenal's tactical discipline turned Anfield from a cauldron into a stalemate, securing a vital three points.

articles.title: Cowboys Injury Woes Mount As Schoonmaker, Clark Face Sunday Test
articles.summary: Two key starters face uncertainty for Sunday's game against Arizona. Get the latest injury updates and what it means for the Cowboys' run game.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys are looking for their first back-to-back wins of the season, but a fresh wave of injuries threatens to derail that momentum just before kickoff. Two key starters are now on the injury report ahead of the Sunday showdown with the Arizona Cardinals at AT&T Stadium. The situation is fluid, with the team releasing updated practice participation numbers on Friday that leave the coaching staff with tough choices.

Defensive tackle Kenny Clark is the most pressing concern for the front seven. He practiced without issues earlier in the week but was limited on Friday due to a back problem. The defensive line's interior remains uncertain as his status is now listed as questionable. On the other side of the ball, tight end Luke Schoonmaker is expected to miss his third straight game. Thursday and Friday practice sessions were missed due to a groin injury, with reports suggesting he is unlikely to play. This leaves the third-string tight end spot empty just as the team tries to find its offensive identity.

Defensive Health Improves While Offense Struggles

While the loss of Clark and Schoonmaker stings, there is genuine hope on the defensive side of the ball. Three players who have been on injured reserve are finally getting back on the field. Friday's practice saw full participation from Safety P.J. Locke, linebacker Marist Liufau, and defensive tackle Jonathan Bullard. They are working through their 21-day practice windows and are listed as questionable for the game. Coach Brian Schottenheimer sees this return as a major turning point for the unit. "The health of this defense is getting us excited. We're getting bodies back, and that's huge for us," Schottenheimer said, according to Yahoo Sports .

These defensive players were needed back after the unit surrendered more than 330 yards in each of the previous two contests. The return of Locke, Liufau, and Bullard adds depth that the team desperately needed. However, the offensive line still faces questions with George Pickens also listed as questionable due to shoulder and hamstring issues. Pickens was limited all week, adding another layer of uncertainty to the receiving corps.

The Cowboys are trying to re-identify who they want to be after a strong 38-21 win over the Eagles. Dak Prescott observed that earlier weeks saw the team lean too heavily on the pass, though the running game offered needed balance. Javonte Williams rushed for a season-high 155 yards in that victory. If Schoonmaker cannot play, the team may have to lean even more on the run game and the fullback position. Coach Schottenheimer highlighted fullback Hunter Luepke as a key player to step up if the tight end depth is depleted.

"He's a guy that we talk a lot about that does just everything good," Schottenheimer said regarding Luepke, according to Dallas News . The coach added that Luepke received a game ball for being dominant on special teams against the Eagles last week. This could mean more three-tight-end sets or heavy packages featuring Luepke to compensate for the loss of the tight end depth. Dallas cannot risk another home loss since Arizona has claimed victory in the last four meetings against the Cowboys.

Although Arizona arrives with a 2-5 record, they defeated Dallas 27-17 last season on Monday night. Prescott has not forgotten that loss and emphasized the need to treat the Cardinals with respect. "Understanding what happened last year, it was an ugly, ugly game, ugly on our part," Prescott told DallasCowboys.com this week, according to Yahoo Sports . He described the recent win as a reset and believes the team is ready for the blitz looks Arizona will bring. The game kicks off at 1 p.m. ET on Sunday, and the health of the roster will be the biggest factor in whether Dallas can finally get over the hump.

articles.title: Iraola to tell Alexander Isak to go to ground next time as Liverpool denied 'clear penalty' in Arsenal loss
articles.summary: Andoni Iraola was out-scrapped by his old pal as Mikel Arteta as Liverpool scratched and clawed but couldn't find an equalizer in a tight and tense 1-0 loss...
articles.body:
Andoni Iraola was out-scrapped by his old pal as Mikel Arteta as Liverpool scratched and clawed but couldn't find an equalizer in a tight and tense 1-0 loss to Arsenal at Anfield on Sunday.

But might it have been 1-1 earlier in the game had Alexander Isak dove to the ground after a clear shirt pull slowed his attempted header of a free kick?

Iraola thinks so, and is lamenting his team's failure to turn dominance into goals, including that non-penalty. Iraola said he'll tell Isak to go to the ground next time, calling the fact that Isak not winning a penalty in part because he didn't dive is "a problem for the game."

The loss leaves Liverpool nine points off the top of the table on a day they could've put themselves into the title conversation by moving three back of Man City and Arsenal.

Andoni Iraola reaction from Liverpool's tight clash with Arsenal

Thoughts on the game: "I liked the attitude. Probably our worst part was until we conceded a goal. The reaction to that was very good. We put them under pressure and had some good chances but couldn't find the equalizer."

Why couldn't you finish chances? "You have to give credit to them. The goal comes when we mess up a goal kick and we still had possession to defend it a lot better. We had 7-8 guys but didn't defend it properly. The players then gave everything."

"There were long periods where we pressed really well, really high. When you are losing 1-0 it gives you less merit because they can be on the defensive side. We won a lot of duels against them and I cannot ask more of my players' willingness to go."

"We had big chances. We hit the cross bar. We had real good chances. We should finish better. This is easy to see but the reason was the start of the game that put them in a big advantage,."

Should you have had a penalty? "The Gakpo one was sustained holding but definitely the Alex [Isak] one was a clear one. They hold the tee shirt and he's going to head the ball in but he doesn't go to the ground."

Should he have gone to the ground? "That's the probnlmwe have in the game because he doesn't dive — the fact that you are asking if he should go to the floor. It is what it is. I should tell Alex next time he has to go to the floor."

Will you tell him that? "Yes definitely."

The Valkyries and the City of San Francisco will host the parade along the city's Embarcadero on Wednesday, Nov. 1.

Fans can begin lining up along the parade route at 9 a.m. on the bay Side of the Embarcadero.

The parade will start at noon and expected to end at 2 p.m.

The parade will start at noon at the Ferry Building, travel along the Embarcadero, and end at King and 2nd streets.

articles.title: Arsenal go top after narrow win at Liverpool
articles.summary: Arsenal pick up their first win at Anfield since 2012 to go three points clear of Man City
articles.body:
Arsenal went three points clear of Manchester City at the top of the English Premier League after a statement 1-0 win at Liverpool.

The Gunners had not won at Anfield since September 2012, when current coach Mikel Arteta captained the away side to a 2-0 victory, and had gone winless in their past 13 visits.

However, Kai Havertz turned home a low cross from Declan Rice after the home side were caught trying to play out from the back to silence the Kop on 16 minutes. The visitors withstood wave after wave of pressure from Andoni Iraola’s side thereafter.

Liverpool responded strongly with Florian Wirtz curling a free kick against the bar and Alexis Mac Allister heading a good chance over.

Arsenal weathered the storm, though, and defended superbly to keep Liverpool largely at arm’s length after the break, denying the home side a shot on target for the second meeting in succession.

Arteta’s side replaces Manchester City at the top with 24 points from nine games, with City on 21 after losing at home to Brighton and Hove Albion on Saturday.

Liverpool’s second league defeat of the season left them nine points behind Arsenal in fifth place.

articles.title: La confesión viral del Dibu Martínez sobre Luis Díaz
articles.standfirst: Dibu Martínez y su sorpresiva declaración sobre Luis Díaz
articles.summary: Dibu Martínez y su sorpresiva declaración sobre Luis Díaz
articles.body: El guardameta argentino Emiliano ‘Dibu’ Martínez volvió a acaparar las tendencias en redes sociales tras una de sus acostumbradas declaraciones sin filtro. En medio de una charla distendida para el espacio digital ‘Los Edul’ —conducido por los reconocidos periodistas argentinos Esteban y Gastón Edul—, el arquero campeón del mundo dejó una frase muy comentada que involucra directamente a la estrella colombiana Luis Díaz. El estilo frontal y desinhibido del portero de la Selección Argentina y del Chelsea generó inmediato eco tanto en el sur del continente como en Colombia, reavivando el interés por los picantes cruces y la alta competitividad que caracteriza a estas dos figuras sudamericanas en la élite del balompié mundial. Durante la entrevista en formato de charla cercana, la conversación giró en torno a los atacantes más desequilibrantes a los que les ha tocado enfrentar en su carrera y los duelos memorables que ha protagonizado vistiendo la camiseta de la Albiceleste. Al ser consultado sobre el extremo colombiano —figura de la Selección Colombia y de gran momento en Europa—, el ‘Dibu’ no escatimó en darle su toque característico a la respuesta, generando reacciones divididas entre los hinchas de uno y otro bando. La pregunta era una de esas clásicas dinámicas de entrevistas deportivas: “¿A qué jugador tienes de hijo?”. Martínez eligió a Luis Díaz sin dudar. La respuesta no fue casual: el portero argentino y el extremo colombiano se han cruzado en partidos de clubes y de selecciones, y sus duelos han dejado episodios memorables en la Premier League y en competiciones sudamericanas. Los enfrentamientos entre Emiliano Martínez y Luis Díaz ya poseen antecedentes de alto voltaje emocional y futbolístico. Desde aquellos inolvidables cruces por las Eliminatorias Sudamericanas y la recordada definición por penales en la Copa América 2021 —donde el ‘Dibu’ se convirtió en héroe de Argentina y el delantero colombiano logró dejar su huella con anotaciones de gran factura—, cada mención mutua acapara portadas. Para los seguidores del fútbol cafetero, el atacante guajiro sigue siendo la carta principal de desequilibrio, mientras que el arquero marplatense se mantiene en el ojo del huracán mediático por sus polémicas, su jerarquía bajo los tres palos y su reciente recuperación tras el fuerte choque sufrido en la Premier League.

articles.title: David Alonso conquista el GP de Malasia de Moto2 tras una gran remontada
articles.standfirst: David Alonso gana el Gran Premio de Malasia de Moto2 y brilla en Sepang
articles.summary: David Alonso gana el Gran Premio de Malasia de Moto2 y brilla en Sepang
articles.body: La bandera de Colombia volvió a ondear en lo más alto del podio internacional del motociclismo. David Alonso firmó una actuación memorable este domingo en el Circuito Internacional de Sepang, quedándose con la victoria en el Gran Premio de Malasia de Moto2 tras una carrera llena de emociones, adelantamientos al límite y sobre saltos físicos que pusieron a prueba su temple. Partiendo desde la cuarta posición de la parrilla de salida, el joven hispano-colombiano demostró una vez más por qué es uno de los talentos más prometedores de la categoría intermedia del Mundial de Motociclismo. Desde el semáforo apagado, la tensión se palpaba en el asfalto malayo. Alonso ganó un puesto en los primeros metros y no tardó en superar a Albert Piqueras para situarse directamente en la estela de su compañero de escuadra y rival directo, Daniel Holgado. Con un ritmo frenético, el piloto del Aspar Team lanzó el ataque decisivo en la sexta vuelta, apoderándose de la primera plaza. Sin embargo, la carrera no estuvo exenta de sobresaltos: Alonso sufrió un momento crítico en una de las curvas, donde estuvo a punto de perder el control de su montura. Gracias a sus reflejos, logró salvar una caída segura y mantener la ventaja necesaria para cruzar la línea de meta en solitario. "No estoy acostumbrado a este tipo de carreras, pero al final hemos podido mantener la presión y conseguir la victoria. Hoy me ha pasado de todo. Ya en la parrilla de salida me ha empezado a sangrar la nariz...", confesó Alonso tras finalizar la prueba, revelando los contratiempos físicos debidos a los cambios de temperatura en Sepang. Con esta victoria en tierras asiáticas, David Alonso celebra su segundo triunfo de la temporada 2026 en la categoría de Moto2, emulando la gran gesta conseguida a finales de junio en el Gran Premio de Países Bajos, sumado a los podios cosechados en República Checa, Austria y Aragón. Sepang se consolidad como un territorio talismán para el colombiano. Tras su paso por Moto3 (donde ganó en 2024) y su podio del año pasado en Moto2, este circuito vuelve a sonreírle. Tras este fin de semana brillante, Alonso escala hasta la cuarta posición de la clasificación general con 191 puntos, superando al propio Daniel Holgado. La pelea por el top 3 del campeonato mundial de Moto2 se enciende de cara al cierre de temporada: Iván Ortolá defiende el tercer cajón provisional a una corta distancia, mientras que Manu González comanda la tabla general con 276.5 unidades.

articles.title: Lincoln Riley has confrontation with Ohio State AD, reads prepared statement to media after huge USC win
articles.summary: The USC Trojans stunned the No. 2 Ohio State Buckeyes just days after a dismal loss to Wisconsin, capping a wild week for Lincoln Riley's program.
articles.body: What a wild week it's been for the USC Trojans. Just last Saturday, it seemed like the Lincoln Riley era in Los Angeles was nearing its end. SC went into Madison as a sizable favorite over the Wisconsin Badgers and laid what can only be described as, charitably, an egg. For the first time in his coaching career, a Lincoln Riley team scored just seven points in a game. There were head-scratching coaching mistakes, including attempting a 58-yard field goal against the wind. Predictably, it did not work, setting Wisconsin up with outstanding field position and a score. The Trojans looked poorly prepared and poorly coached, with senior quarterback Jayden Maiava taking multiple atrocious intentional grounding penalties and throwing two picks, a muffed catch on a Badgers kickoff leading to a missed opportunity before halftime, not calling timeout when the SC defense was misaligned on a pivotal fourth-and-2, leading to a Wisconsin touchdown, and an incredible -17 net rushing yards. AFTER YET ANOTHER INEXCUSABLE LOSS TO WISCONSIN, THE LINCOLN RILEY ERA AT USC LOOKS TO BE NEARING AN END After the game, the speculation and discussion was immediate. Riley was mentally checked out in LA, was one common sentiment. USC's athletic department had already started putting together funds to potentially clear Riley's rumored $70 million buyout. And fans and analysts were putting together wish lists of potential new coaches for 2027 and beyond. Then, Saturday happened. USC hosted the Ohio State Buckeyes, still heavily favored despite starting backup quarterback Luke Fahey. OSU has a top three defense, arguably the best player in the country in Jeremiah Smith, and a wealth of big game experience under head coach Ryan Day. And sure enough, the Trojans dominated. Even in a college football season where parity has been more obvious than ever, it was a shocking upset. Ohio State dominated time of possession and racked up yardage thanks to some garbage time drives, but never really looked like they had much of a chance. When set up with a first-and-goal inside the 1-yard-line, the Buckeyes still couldn't get in the end zone. USC, which has been unimpressive for most of the season, looked like a totally different team. Star freshman Trent Mosley took a screen pass on the second play of the game for a long touchdown. Mark Bowman provided the highlight of the year from a tight end, hurdling an Ohio State defender and running through tackles on a huge catch and run. And the Trojans much-maligned defense grabbed an opportune turnover, forced a fumble that was inexplicably not reviewed, and got stop after stop when they needed it. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Needless to say, a win over the number two team in the country was a season, and potentially program, altering turn of events. And Riley had a well, interesting, time after the conclusion, including a run-in with the Ohio State athletic director, and an unusual prepared statement that he read during postgame media availability. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Buckeyes staff and players were walking off the Coliseum field in the tunnel, and Riley tried to walk to the same area with his family and security guard. But an OSU staffer held him up, and after a few seconds, athletic director Ross Bjork can be seen gesturing back toward Riley and saying something toward him. Whatever it was, Riley was not happy about it, clearly saying some very profane phrases back as he was finally let through. Another angle more clearly showed Bjork saying something indistinguishable as he left the field. Confrontations happen, particularly after a heated game between two proud programs. Things got even a bit more unusual though, in the news conference. LINCOLN RILEY ADDRESSES SPECULATION ABOUT HIS FUTURE AT USC AHEAD OF HUGE GAME AGAINST OHIO STATE Riley, who already addressed speculation about his commitment to USC in a midweek news conference, saying LA is where he wants to be, read a prepared statement about his job and the Trojans program. This time, clearly with a bit more, shall we say, fesity language toward the media. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD "This program is built on internal joy, not external applause," he said. "This win is for all the staff members, the players, the leaders, admin, all the people within the walls. I said before this game that I'm the right person for this job, and as long as all those people know that, that's all I care about. I appreciate being part of this university, and all it does. I appreciate our kids and our staff, and I'm going to continue to fight on because that's what being a Trojan is all about. Adios." Not exactly what you'd expect to hear from a head coach coming off a huge win over the No. 2 ranked Ohio State Buckeyes, but it's hard to blame him for being a bit more defense than usual. Riley's faced a long list of questions about his job status the past few weeks, but again, those questions are legitimate. USC's two losses this year were inexcusable. The Oregon Ducks are far from the team most expected in the preseason, and the Trojans defense let backup Dylan Raiola walk all over them in a 41-27 loss. That Wisconsin performance was dreadful, and looks even worse with the Badgers' 30-0 loss to Iowa on Saturday. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER There have been few signature wins in the Riley era, until this one, and after an offseason marketing campaign revolving around the "championship window" now being open, sitting at 6-2 with their season on the brink is simply not good enough. But he deserves credit for the OSU win and how it played out. USC looked like a different team; prepared, focused, intense, and aggressive. Why they don't always look like that? Nobody knows. There are more questions moving forward though, because there always are. How do the Trojans, and Riley, respond in the final three games? The schedule doesn't get easier, with a trip to play the Indiana Hoosiers in Bloomington next week, and a date with the now-No. 5 UCLA Bruins at the Rose Bowl to close out the season. Win out, and the Trojans would almost certainly be in the College Football Playoff, boasting one of the best resumes in the country with three wins over top-5 teams. Lose two of the last three to Indiana and UCLA and finish 8-4? We might be talking about Riley's buyout and that open job at Baylor all over again.

articles.title: Lions All-Pro LB Jack Campbell placed on backboard, carted off field after a tackle against Vikings
articles.summary: Detroit Lions All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell was placed on a backboard and carted off the field early in the fourth quarter against the Minnesota Vikings.
articles.body: Detroit Lions All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell was placed on a backboard and carted off the field early in the fourth quarter against the Minnesota Vikings. He was taken to a hospital to be evaluated for a neck injury and coach Dan Campbell said he did not have any additional information following a 19-15 win against Minnesota. “We’re thinking about him,” he said. Campbell was face down on the turf and was not moving after hitting tight end T.J. Hockenson for his third tackle of the game. He was evaluated by medical personnel before being strapped to a board and carefully lifted onto a court to a round of applause. Detroit’s entire team and most of the coaching staff surrounded the cart before it transported Campbell off the field for further evaluation. The former Iowa star was drafted by the Lions with No. 18 overall pick in 2023. Last season, Campbell was an All-Pro selection after becoming the first NFL player in seven years to have 150-plus tackles and at least five sacks and three forced fumbles. The Lions signed Campbell last May to a four-year contract extension that runs through the 2030 season.

articles.title: Florida State fires Mike Norvell after 6-plus seasons and takes on his nearly $50M buyout
articles.summary: Florida State fired coach Mike Norvell on Sunday, roughly 12 hours after a home loss to Clemson and despite a buyout of roughly $50 million that is among the largest in college football history.
articles.body: TALLAHASSEE, Fla. — Florida State fired coach Mike Norvell on Sunday, roughly 12 hours after a home loss to Clemson and despite a buyout of roughly $50 million that is among the largest in college football history. Norvell and the Seminoles are 10-22 since the start of the 2024 season, and Norvell’s hand-picked quarterbacks — DJ Uiagalelei, Tommy Castellanos and Ashton Daniels — all struggled with accuracy. “We have made the decision to change the leadership of our football program,” school president Richard McCullough said. “We thank Mike Norvell for his commitment and service to Florida State and wish him and his family the very best. We understand the deep passion of Seminole fans and share their high expectations for this program.” Assistant coach Rick Stockstill was named interim head coach while a search for Norvell’s successor plays out. Florida State is 1-5 against Power Four programs this fall, including Saturday’s 36-24 loss to Clemson in which the Seminoles were a 5-point favorite. The Seminoles have not defeated one of their main three rivals — Miami, Florida or Clemson — since the 2023 season. Norvell went 41-39 in his six-plus seasons in Tallahassee, including stunning losses to then-lower-division Jacksonville State in 2021 and Memphis in 2024. Norvell was 24-30 in Atlantic Coast Conference games since 2020. His team’s incredible run three years ago to a 13-0 record — only to be left out of the College Football Playoff — seems long ago now. His buyout is roughly $47 million, which is 85% of his remaining salary through the end of his contract that runs through the 2031 season. His contract does include offset language that would mitigate some of the buyout if he lands another job. Norvell was scheduled to make $10.3 million in 2026. Buying out his assistants would push the buyout far past $50 million. The combined buyouts for Maryland’s Mike Locksley, N.C. State’s Dave Doeren and Baylor’s Dave Aranda are less than Norvell’s total. Florida State’s opening is now the fourth among Power Four schools. Florida State (3-5, 1-4 ACC) plays at Boston College (4-4, 2-3) on Saturday. Even with a competitive player-acquisition budget compared to ACC schools, Florida State won just five Power Four games in the last 2 1/2 seasons. The Seminoles suffered back-to-back losing seasons and are scrambling to become bowl eligible this fall with an interim head coach. The school fired athletic director Michael Alford in mid-September. McCullough issued a statement last Tuesday acknowledging fans’ frustration. “We are not asking you to ignore the results,” McCullough wrote. “We are committed to changing them. And we are not asking you to believe that everything is fine. We know it isn’t.” Florida State has mostly struggled since 2015, going 44-49 under Jimbo Fisher, Willie Taggart and Norvell. The ‘Noles did win 19 consecutive games between the middle of the 2022 season and the ACC title game in December 2023, a stretch that landed Norvell a new contract.

articles.title: Jonathan Taylor's Colts career potentially ends in embarrassment as Jaguars blow out AFC South rivals
articles.summary: Jonathan Taylor's dismal 23-yard performance against Jacksonville may have been his Colts farewell as trade rumors link him to the Giants and Vikings.
articles.body: If that's the last time we saw Jonathan Taylor in an Indianapolis Colts uniform, it was an ugly ending. Their AFC South rivals, the Jacksonville Jaguars, wiped the floor with a 42-7 victory just as trade speculation for the star running back has heated up. The now 2-6 Colts have been making moves during a poor season, albeit without their first-round pick. They just traded away Quenton Nelson, and Taylor remains the most valuable and best player on the roster. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Rumors have swirled that amid sitting in first place in their respective divisions, the New York Giants and Minnesota Vikings could land Taylor, who has made three Pro Bowls. Taylor was bottled up most of the day against Jacksonville, finishing with 23 yards on eight carries and getting saddled with a fumble on a botched trick play. He is the last player to top 100 yards rushing in a game against the Jaguars, accomplishing the feat in the 2024 regular-season finale. Trevor Lawrence threw three touchdowns, Bayshul Tuten scored twice, and Rayuan Lane returned an interception 92 yards for a touchdown with 10 seconds to play in the second quarter. PACKERS' INTEREST IN JONATHAN TAYLOR SHOWS DESIRE TO MOVE ON FROM JOSH JACOBS AND HIS DOMESTIC ABUSE ISSUES Jacksonville’s 28-0 lead was the third-largest advantage at halftime in franchise history. It came five days after the Colts traded two of their best players in Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner. They have reportedly turned down an offer that circled around a second-round pick. Indianapolis last won at EverBank Stadium in 2014. The 12-game skid includes a trip to London in 2016. Even during some of the Jaguars’ worst years — a one-win campaign in 2020 and a pair of three-win seasons — they managed to beat the Colts at home. Daniel Jones completed 19 of 28 passes for 144 yards, with a touchdown to Josh Downs and two interceptions. He was benched in the fourth quarter and replaced by Anthony Richardson. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER Indianapolis will host the Dallas Cowboys next week, but it remains to be seen whether Taylor will be there. The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.title: Fallon Sherrock hits back at critics after beating Luke Littler to win £501,000 on Netflix, revealing why she was eligible despite her darts success
articles.summary: Fallon Sherrock has turned a night of criticism into a career-defining victory, leaving Luke Littler stunned and walking away with a staggering £501,000
articles.body: Fallon Sherrock has turned a night of criticism into a career-defining victory, leaving Luke Littler stunned and walking away with a staggering £501,000 prize. The English darts star delivered when it mattered most, ending Littler's winning run in Netflix's high-stakes challenge. Yet her triumph sparked another debate, with viewers questioning why an accomplished player was allowed to compete against the world champion in an event featuring amateur challengers. Sherrock has now broken her silence, explaining the eligibility rule that secured her place and making it clear that she had every right to seize the opportunity.Fallon Sherrock responds to criticism after stunning Luke LittlerSherrock's victory came during Netflix's live darts special, Beat Luke Littler, held at Manchester Central on Friday, October 30. The concept was straightforward but carried enormous stakes. Challengers had to defeat the reigning world champion in a single leg of 501 to take home £501,000. Littler had already survived 14 opponents when Sherrock finally stepped up.The 32-year-old knew the challenge was unlike a regular tournament. One mistake could end her hopes, while a perfect opportunity could change her life. She made the most of it.However, her appearance had attracted attention long before the competition began. Sherrock is not an unknown name in darts. She has built a reputation through years of competition and historic achievements, making her inclusion alongside everyday players a talking point among fans.Some viewers questioned whether someone with her experience should have been included in an event presented as a contest for amateur players. Others felt her achievements made the competition less balanced.Sherrock was aware of the negative reaction and admitted that the comments had been difficult to ignore."I mean it's been tough," she said. "Because obviously I do see the backlash and I do see all the negative comments. But at the end of the day, I fit the criteria for this. I've never had a tour card, and I wouldn't class myself as a pro really, because all I do is just play darts for the enjoyment of it."She also reminded critics that her journey in the sport began at a very different level."I think people forget where I started off as well. When I won at the Worlds, I was still just doing WDF (World Darts Federation). I'm just so happy to overcome all the hate and win."Her comments addressed the main question surrounding her participation. Despite her reputation, she had never held a Professional Darts Corporation (PDC) Tour Card, which was the key eligibility requirement for the Netflix competition.Why Fallon Sherrock was eligible for the £501,000 Netflix challengeThe controversy largely came down to the difference between being an established darts player and holding professional status under the PDC system.Sherrock has competed at major events, earned international recognition and become one of the most familiar faces in women's darts. However, the Netflix competition did not simply exclude everyone with previous tournament experience.The eligibility rules centred on PDC Tour Card status. Anyone who had never held one could qualify, even if they had enjoyed considerable success elsewhere in the sport.That distinction worked in Sherrock's favour.Her career has included appearances at the PDC World Darts Championship and success on the women's circuit. She also won the inaugural Women's World Matchplay in 2022. Yet those achievements did not automatically make her ineligible under Netflix's rules.The organisers wanted a field that could offer Littler a genuine challenge rather than a series of predictable matches. Sherrock's experience made her a strong competitor, but her lack of a PDC Tour Card kept her within the stated eligibility criteria.PDC president Barry Hearn also stepped forward to defend the decision. Hearn, who was involved in the selection process, rejected suggestions that Sherrock should have been left out because of her reputation.Asked whether her inclusion was unfair, he responded:"No, not at all," said Hearn. "She's not a PDC Tour Card holder. She's entitled to enter. Why should she be denied?"He also explained why having skilled opponents was important to the entertainment value of the event."She's a well-known player and she's a very good player. But Mitchell Lawrie is a very well-known player and an excellent player."Do you want just a series of 20 matches where someone can't even throw a dart? No, of course we want excellence competing against excellence, and that's what it was all about."His defence highlighted an important point. The competition was designed to test Littler, not simply provide him with easy victories.How Fallon Sherrock beat Luke Littler to claim £501,000While the eligibility debate continued outside the arena, Sherrock had a much bigger task waiting at the oche.Littler entered the competition as the clear favourite. The two-time world champion had already demonstrated his quality by defeating the first 14 challengers, with several opponents struggling to put him under serious pressure.One contestant, Irish student Pearse Mackle, came particularly close. He had an opportunity to take the £501,000 prize but missed the bullseye needed to complete his finish.Sherrock became the 15th challenger to face the teenager. She won the bull-off, securing the advantage of throwing first, and quickly made her intentions clear.The Englishwoman opened with a solid scoring visit before producing a crucial 180. That maximum gave her the momentum and left her with just 43 points after 12 darts.Littler, meanwhile, was unable to match her scoring pace. He still had a difficult 142-point finish in front of him when Sherrock stepped up to close the contest.She missed her first attempt at double top but kept her composure and landed the next dart.That was it.The crowd erupted as Sherrock realised she had beaten the world's best player and secured £501,000. The victory also ended the entire competition, as the format required the show to stop once someone defeated Littler.The prize was particularly significant. It represented the biggest payday of Sherrock's career and the second-largest single prize in darts history, behind the £1 million Littler received for winning his second world championship.The moment became even more special because her son, Rory, was present to witness the achievement.Speaking to host Gary Lineker after the win, Sherrock struggled to describe her emotions."I can’t put into words how much this means."I’m really lost for words right now. It was a great moment. Give me an opportunity and I’ll take it every time. I’m really proud of myself."Luke Littler praises Fallon Sherrock after Netflix defeatLittler did not hide his disappointment at losing, but he was quick to acknowledge the quality of Sherrock's performance.The teenager had controlled most of the evening and looked comfortable against the earlier challengers. However, the one-leg format left little room for recovery once Sherrock found her rhythm.He praised her ability to finish the match despite missing her first attempt at double top."Brilliant. That’s what one person had to do, win the bull and go out with 15 and that’s exactly what Fallon did. When she missed the first double top I thought, ‘give me a chance’. But she didn’t. World class."Littler also appeared pleased with the overall experience and hinted that he would welcome another edition."I’ve enjoyed every bit of it," Littler said afterwards. "Everything leading up to this. Maybe, Netflix, we can do it again next year?"For Sherrock, however, the night carried a different meaning. She had faced criticism over whether she belonged in the competition, but she answered those questions with her performance.Her victory also brought fresh attention to women's darts and demonstrated the level of talent competing outside the PDC Tour Card system.The debate over her eligibility may continue, but the rules were clear, and Sherrock met them. She earned her place, faced Littler and delivered when the opportunity arrived.At 32, the Queen of the Palace now has another remarkable chapter in her career, along with a £501,000 reward for proving that one opportunity can change everything.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Lando Norris says Kimi Antonelli should celebrate F1 title “properly” after breakthrough season
articles.summary: The outgoing world champion says the Mercedes driver “deserves it an incredible amount” after becoming F1’s youngest-ever title winner in Mexico
articles.body:
Antonelli finished third behind Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez to clinch the title with four races to spare, becoming the youngest champion in Formula 1's history at just 20 years and 68 days old.

Norris, who won his first title with McLaren last year and finished fifth in Mexico, said after the race that he was delighted for the Italian.

"I mean, he deserves it. It's been insane this year. That's an understatement," he said. "So, congrats to him, especially at his age. To win it is pretty incredibly impressive."

The Briton added that he hoped the driver would truly celebrate this special moment, despite his young age.

"I'm very, very happy for him. He's a lovely, lovely guy. He deserves it an incredible amount, and I hope even though he's young, he goes out and celebrates it properly," he said.

"He's had an outstanding season. So, yeah, just very happy for him."

Norris has been full of praise for Antonelli for a number of weeks now. Speaking in Austin, he commented on how quickly he'd been able to master his Mercedes machinery, even compared to his experienced team-mate George Russell .

"I think it's very impressive what he's been able to do at his age, his second year in Formula 1. He's going to be the youngest world champion ever. It's pretty, pretty incredible," he said.

"I rate George and I think he's a very good driver. But Kimi has been two levels above George the whole season. So, you know, he's done a pretty incredible job."

Antonelli has won nine races this season and leads the drivers' standings on 380 points, 119 clear of Verstappen. Russell, who started the year as the title favourite, is fourth.

Norris, meanwhile, has struggled in his defence of the title, with only two race wins in the Hungarian and Dutch Grands Prix.

He said ahead of the Mexico weekend that he would gladly give up his status as champion.

"I have nothing but respect for Kimi. He's a very nice guy. We get along very well and I'm more than happy to pass the No 1 over to him," Norris said.

articles.body:
Joan Beringer left San Antonio thinking about everything he had failed to do. Victor Wembanyama offered a different assessment of the Timberwolves teenager.

Starting in place of Rudy Gobert on Saturday, Beringer spent 34 minutes dealing with one of basketball's toughest assignments. Wembanyama finished with 43 points and six blocks in a 121-111 Spurs victory. Beringer finished frustrated.

"Just that I couldn't really stop Wemby. I couldn't really stop him," Beringer said . "A lot of frustration, but we have to think about next."

For a 19-year-old still learning the position, the performance contained plenty worth taking into the next game. Beringer scored 12 points, grabbed six rebounds and contributed two assists while Minnesota played without Gobert, Anthony Edwards and Donte DiVincenzo. But the strongest endorsement came from the player who had made his night so difficult.

"He acts like a player who knows what it takes to stay and last in the league," Wembanyama said . "From what I hear, he has a good work ethic, real seriousness, and humility. He has a great future."

That praise addressed qualities Minnesota will need long after the disappointment of this loss fades. Beringer is being asked to learn quickly, contribute immediately and handle mistakes without allowing them to consume his next possession. Saturday showed how difficult that balance can be.

Beringer acknowledged that greater physicality could help him against Wembanyama, then criticized himself for failing to provide enough of it. He recognized a potential answer but felt he had not applied it consistently.

Jonathan Kuminga noticed how heavily those shortcomings were weighing on him. During the game, Kuminga pulled Beringer aside to offer guidance. Afterward, he explained why.

"I think he's doing so much good that he's not realizing that he's doing a lot of good stuff," Kuminga said . "He's just trying to penalize himself on small stuff."

Kuminga understood the impulse. He described wanting to be perfect early in his own career, when limited opportunities made every mistake feel especially costly. His advice was to trust the work, learn from different coverages and keep playing. That perspective matters for Beringer because the opportunities are arriving much faster now.

Beringer played just 314 minutes as a rookie, spending most of the year redshirting. Seven games into this season, he had already surpassed 130.

Gobert's absence with back spasms pushed him into a starting assignment against Wembanyama on the second night of a back-to-back. Minnesota was also completing its fifth game in seven nights.

Beringer still wanted the conversation to center on winning. He believed the players available were capable of it. That expectation helps explain his frustration, even as teammates and coaches saw reasons for encouragement.

"He battled," Chris Finch said . "Got his hands full for sure, but he battled and did some good things."

Finch had identified progress a night earlier, after Minnesota's win over the Clippers. Beringer was learning to control the activity that makes him useful.

"He always plays hard and he goes after everything, and that's what we love about him," Finch explained. "But sometimes his overaggressiveness will put him in foul trouble."

The next step is choosing those moments more effectively. Against San Antonio, Beringer committed five fouls but stayed available long enough to give Minnesota substantial minutes at a position where its options were limited. LaMelo Ball sees those experiences as necessary preparation. He praised Beringer's talent while emphasizing the smaller details they can improve together.

"It's early in the season, so I feel like we're going to definitely need [him] a lot," Ball said . "It's just all reps and helping."

Minnesota needs Beringer to absorb those lessons without losing the aggression that earned him this opportunity. Kuminga is helping him recognize progress. Finch is helping him direct his energy. Ball wants to sharpen their connection.

And the opponent Beringer couldn't stop sees a player preparing himself for a long NBA career.

articles.title: William Byron Dominates Martinsville to Claim His First Win of the 2026 Season
articles.summary: William Byron picked one of the biggest weekends of the NASCAR season to finally get back to Victory Lane. The Hendrick Motorsports driver dominated Sunday’s...
articles.body:
William Byron picked one of the biggest weekends of the NASCAR season to finally get back to Victory Lane.

The Hendrick Motorsports driver dominated Sunday's Xfinity 500 at Martinsville Speedway , earning his first NASCAR Cup Series win of the 2026 season in the 35th race of the year.

Byron led a race-high 362 of 500 laps , won both stages, and controlled much of the afternoon at the paperclip. He put the No. 24 Chevrolet out front and consistently kept the competition behind him.

His biggest challenge came from teammate Chase Elliott, who made a late push in the closing laps. Elliott managed to close the gap, but Byron held him off and crossed the finish line 2.049 seconds ahead .

It was a massive day for Hendrick Motorsports, with Elliott finishing second to give the organization a 1-2 finish. Ty Gibbs finished third, followed by Josh Berry and Shane van Gisbergen.

For Byron, this marked his 17th career Cup Series victory, fourth win at Martinsville, and seventh consecutive season with at least one victory . After going winless through the first 34 races, he finally got the breakthrough he had been looking for.

But Byron's victory also had major championship implications.

Kyle Larson entered Martinsville with an opportunity to clinch the 2026 championship one race early. However, his ninth-place finish kept the title fight alive heading into next weekend's finale at Homestead-Miami Speedway.

Denny Hamlin finished sixth, while Christopher Bell finished 10th. Larson still holds a significant advantage, but the championship is not officially decided yet.

Byron may not be competing for the championship himself, but he just delivered a reminder of how dangerous this Hendrick Motorsports organization can be.

Winning at Martinsville is never easy, but leading 362 laps and controlling the race from start to finish is an entirely different statement.

With just one race remaining in the 2026 season, Byron has finally found Victory Lane again, and Hendrick Motorsports is heading into the finale with plenty of momentum.

articles.title: Patriots cut Dolphins lead to 13-10 on Kyle Williams touchdown
articles.summary: The Patriots are back within a field goal in Miami.
articles.body:
The Patriots are back within a field goal in Miami.

Quarterback Drake Maye hit wide receiver Kyle Williams with a deep pass that Williams appeared to take into the end zone before losing control of the ball. Officials ruled the play an incompletion, however, and Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel had to throw a challenge flag to get the call corrected.

Andy Borregales's extra point cut the Dolphins's lead to 13-10 with 9:23 to play in the third quarter.

Maye is now 9-of-12 for 100 yards and Williams is up to two touchdowns on the season. Tight end Hunter Henry has not returned to the game since hurting his foot in the first half, which has left the Patriots even shorter on options after making wide receiver A.J. Brown inactive ahead of the game.

articles.title: Nil Llop revela que sufrió una mielitis: "Nadie sabe lo que he pasado"
articles.standfirst: El patinador olímpico tuvo que ser hospitalizado de urgencia
articles.summary: El patinador olímpico tuvo que ser hospitalizado de urgencia
articles.body: El pasado mes de septiembre Nil Llop Izquierdo, que en Milán-Cortina 2026 fue el primer español que consiguió competir en patinaje de velocidad en unos Juegos Olímpicos, debió ser hospitalizado en los Países Bajos debido a una grave inflamación de la médula espinal provocada por una infección. Se encontraba preparando la próxima temporada con su nuevo equipo profesional, el Team X²O Badkamers. La dolencia resultó ser una mielitis: la inflamación de la médula espinal que interrumpe las vías nerviosas que comunican el cerebro con el resto del cuerpo. El tratamiento de Nil comenzó de inmediato con previsión de ser trasladado a un hospital especializado en España para seguir con su recuperación cerca de los suyos. Ahora, el deportista ha realizado su primera comunicación pública, a través de sus redes sociales. Una comunicación tranquilizadora porque se le puede ver realizar ejercicios de rehabilitación, aunque relata lo duro del proceso. Nil confiesa que le enfermedad le acometió en un gran momento personal: "por fin conseguí que me fichara un equipo profesional en Holanda, me había mudado con mi novia y estaba cumpliendo todo por lo que llevaba tantos años luchando. Y, de repente, una mielitis lo cambió todo. Pasé de estar viviendo mi sueño a estar paralizado, sin poder moverme y teniendo que aprender de nuevo cosas tan básicas como caminar. Han sido días muy duros, de mucho miedo, de incertidumbre y de preguntarme muchas veces por qué a mí. He tenido días en los que lo he visto todo muy oscuro. Nadie sabe realmente lo que he pasado, ni física ni mentalmente. Y todavía hay muchas cosas que no sé: si volveré a patinar como antes, si podré volver a competir o si algún día alcanzaré un nivel mejor. Pero hay algo que sí tengo claro: voy a luchar cada día por volver a encontrar mi mejor versión, sea cual sea. Este proceso me está enseñando a valorar cosas que antes daba por hechas. Levantarme, caminar, poder hacer mi vida… cosas que parecen tan normales y que, de repente, se convierten en un auténtico privilegio. Estoy aprendiendo a disfrutar del día a día, a dar el 100 % en cada cosa que hago y a entender que no todo depende de los resultados. Porque al final, da igual lo que hayas conseguido, los sueños que hayas cumplido o quién seas. Sin salud, no hay nada. Y cuando te toca vivir algo así, también te das cuenta de que hay mucha gente, joven y no tan joven, que lleva años luchando contra situaciones muy difíciles. Hoy solo quiero seguir avanzando, paso a paso, disfrutando de cada pequeño progreso y sin dejar de luchar por mis sueños. Gracias a mi familia, a mi padre, a mi novia, mis hermanas, a Sandra y a mi equipo @teamx2obadkamers @cpvelprat. Por otra parte agradecer también al CSD, COE, Consell Catala de l’Esport, RFEDH, Fceh en especial a Xavi Cherta, Mónica Bosch, David Samper, Anna Soldevila, Carles Giralt y Frank González por estar a mi lado en los días en los que ni yo mismo sabía cómo seguir. No sé cómo será el camino que viene, pero sé que no voy a recorrerlo solo". El deportista acaba su comunicado con el emoticón de un corazón herido y curado. Lo que está claro es que puede contar con el apoyo y la solidaridad de todo el deporte español.

articles.title: Biggest winners, losers from Steelers' Week 8 victory over Browns
articles.summary: Here's a look at the biggest winners and losers from the Pittsburgh Steelers' Week 8 matchup against the Cleveland Browns.
articles.body:
The Browns is the Browns. All jokes aside, the Pittsburgh Steelers advanced to 6-2 on the regular season and have taken the No. 1 spot in the AFC North following their Week 8 win over Cleveland. And there are plenty of studs — and duds — to recognize from Pittsburgh's victory.

From running back dominance to a huge game for the defense, here's a look at the biggest winners and losers from the Steelers' Week 8 win over the Browns.

Wow. Warren finished the game with 143 rushing yards on just 17 attempts, an incredible 8.4 yards per attempt, in addition to one rushing touchdown. I hope no one is getting tired of seeing Warren make the winners list every week, as I have a feeling the talented Steelers running back is just getting started.

Washington is the definition of a 6-foot-7 freight train that just so happens to be good at football. Washington hauled in three passes for 98 yards, including a game-changing 58-yard catch-and-run that set up a Pittsburgh touchdown.

Patrick Queen and Payton Wilson's hot streak continues, as the starting linebacker duo dominated the Browns in the Steelers' Week 8 win. Combining for 20 combined tackles, two tackles for loss, 1.5 sacks, two QB hits, and a forced fumble (most of which came from Queen), the Steelers linebackers went from being an area of concern to becoming arguably a top-five unit in the league.

Ben Roethlisberger may own the Browns, but T.J. Watt is becoming a close second. Watt finished the game with two sacks, two tackles for loss, three QB hits, and one pass defended. Pittsburgh's pass rush as a whole also deserves credit, as they were on Deshaun Watson all game, recording a total of eight team sacks.

Metcalf, Metcalf, Metcalf… At this point, it almost feels redundant to keep adding him to this list. Why should fans expect anything different? Metcalf hauled in just one pass for four yards, despite being targeted six times. He was responsible for a costly drop that resulted in an interception for the Browns. The Steelers didn't pay Metcalf $132 million to play like this.

Honorable mention: Browns DE Jared Verse

I would be remiss if I didn't include Verse, who would honestly be the biggest loser on this list if it weren't a Steelers-only analysis. Verse talked a lot of trash following Cleveland's fluke win back in Week 4, and was making bold claims about beating Pittsburgh all week. Well, Verse finished the game with just one tackle and zero sacks, a reoccurring theme for the sackless Browns defender. Oh, and he got body-slammed by Steelers offensive lineman Mason McCormick.

articles.title: Jaguars-Colts report card gives out high marks for efficiency, defense
articles.summary: Grading the Jacksonville Jaguars game vs. the Indianapolis Colts.
articles.body:
Report card on the Jacksonville Jaguars' 42-7 rout of the Indianapolis Colts , at EverBank Stadium.

The Jaguars have a short week and go back on the road for a Thursday night game on Nov. 5 at the Baltimore Ravens . The next three games will be on the road before the Jaguars return home on Nov. 29 vs. Tennessee.

Jaguars vs. Colts: See second-half scenes from EverBank Stadium

The Jaguars played to the elements and utilized running backs Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez running and receiving. Tuten became the first Jaguars back in team history to rush for more than 100 yards (104), catch passes for more 50 yards (two for 55, and score a TD both ways. Rodriguez added 41 yards and both players gave coach Liam Coen the burst he was looking for from the running game.

QB Trevor Lawrence was sacked three times and he fumbled the ball away once, dropping the grade down a notch. In fairness, the offensive line had to be shuffled again but the strip-sack came after OT Cole Van Lanen , usually their steadiest lineman, got fooled on an inside move by the Colts' Jaylan Tuimoloau. But Lawrence was otherwise efficient, spreading his 10 completions among eight receivers.

Because of the emphasis on running the ball out of multiple tight-end sets, the Jags' wide receivers had a quiet day. But Brian Thomas Jr., opened the scoring with a 12-yard TD reception, and as a group they all blocked well.

Given the early injuries to S Eric Murray and NT DaVon Hamilton , the defense turned in a superb job and never allowed the Colts an answer. The pass rush returned with four sacks and 10 quarterback hits, and who had the following players getting turnovers on their bingo card: Rayuan Lane (92-yard interception return), Branson Combs and rookie edge rusher Bryan Thomas Jr. Colts RB Jonathan Taylor has yet to rush for 100 yards in Jacksonville and after a 19-yard run on the Colts' first offensive play, he had only seven carries for 4 yards.

No need for Cam Little to produce a 60-yard field goal this week. Punter Logan Cooke averaged 48.7 yards on a season-high six attempts and had punts downed or fair-caught inside the 6-yard line three times. Branson Combs had a couple of big special teams hits. Kickoff return defense remains a bit bothersome.

The mark of a Liam Coen-coached Jaguars team so far is that the team wins the games they're supposed to win. The Jags were double-digit favorites over an opponent in disarray and took care of business. The injuries to Hamilton and Cleveland may be costly down the road, but only if the front office doesn't address it, which they likely will.

The Jaguars also had their fewest penalty yards (65) since week three against New England.

Coen has said several times this season that it's crucial that the team win all six games in Jacksonville. They're halfway there.
