articles.title: Texas is banged up after win over Mississippi State
articles.summary: Five key plays were unable to finish Saturday’s game.
articles.body:
Already without star pass rusher Colin Simmons for a second straight game, the Texas Longhorns suffered more attrition during Saturday's 31-3 win over the Mississippi State Bulldogs when numerous players left the game and did not return.

"Graceson Littleton didn't finish the game. Cam Coleman didn't finish the game. Kade Phillips didn't finish the game. Hollywood Smothers didn't finish the game. Ryan Wingo didn't finish the game. So, all integral parts of the team," Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian said after the game.

Littleton only played 10 snaps before spending the rest of the game on the sideline without his helmet. After trying to get loose at halftime, Littleton was not able to return as senior cornerback Bo Mascoe moved to nickel.

Coleman also played 10 snaps before leaving the game, by which point he'd already impacted the with a 47-yard catch and run on the opening drive that he finished with a 14-yard touchdown reception. The Auburn transfer spent the second half in street clothes after trying to return from the shoulder injury he sustained against Ole Miss last week.

Phillips played 27 snaps, forcing freshman Smoke Matthews to see the most significant action of his career, recording two tackles in 39 snaps while allowing one catch for eight yards on two targets.

Smothers briefly made his return after missing the Ole Miss win with a shoulder injury, playing 14 snaps and losing six yards on four carries before he was helped off the field and went into the medical tent.

Wingo was able to play 42 snaps before leaving, recording three catches for 14 yards on six targets.

Sarkisian did not immediately know whether any of the injuries are serious.

"The severity of all those guys' injuries is unknown at the moment," he said.

According to Anwar Richardson of Orangebloods on Sunday, the prognosis is not positive for most of the injured players.

The season's only bye week came after the conference opener, leaving the Longhorns halfway through its stretch of eight games in eight weeks to end the season, what is already brutal to be a brutal stretch as Texas navigates a nine-game SEC schedule for the first time.

So the staff is likely to make some adjustments about how they practice to ensure that the injured players can return as quickly as possible and to ensure that everyone else is as healthy as possible, because all the players who are seeing significant snaps have some type of knock.

Put quarterback Arch Manning fully in that category after taking some big hits against Mississippi State — Manning was sacked five times, forced to scramble three times, and had four designed runs. Manning spent most of the game with a bloody hand.

"I don't want him to have to endure that," Sarkisian said. "I don't want a bloody hand and him getting sacked five times. That's not a recipe for success. Is he going to run it some? Yes. Do I think that's part of his game? Yes. But there's a line we got to be careful we don't cross over with him, because we need him as healthy as he can be moving forward."

Regaining some health with be a priority for the Longhorns before heading to Columbia.

"When I talk about what's going to be the emphasis for this week, one of them is not only getting these guys back, but obviously Colin. The more of these guys we can get back, the better team we're going to be, right?" Sarkisian said.

"And so that recovery has to start now for a lot of these guys. What are they doing right now after the game to start that process, and then into tomorrow and early in the week? We'll have a better gauge midweek of where everybody is and what that looks like."

articles.title: Denny Hamlin Makes Painful Admission After Martinsville Championship Setback
articles.summary: Denny Hamlin entered Martinsville needing a big result to revive his championship hopes. After a frustrating afternoon, he admitted the title was slipping ou...
articles.body:
Denny Hamlin arrived at Martinsville Speedway needing something special to keep his NASCAR Cup Series championship hopes alive. Instead, he left knowing his best opportunity to close the gap had slipped away.

The six-time Martinsville winner entered Sunday's Xfinity 500 trailing Kyle Larson by 73 points in the standings. He needed a big afternoon at one of his strongest tracks, but a costly opening stage and subsequent contact left him fighting to recover rather than challenging for the victory.

Afterward, Hamlin wasn't interested in pretending the championship picture looked any better than it did.

"For us this weekend, everything to gain, nothing to lose," Hamlin said during his post-race interview. "We just didn't gain enough to make it realistic."

It was a difficult admission from a driver who had entered the weekend believing Martinsville offered a genuine opportunity to change the direction of his title pursuit.

Hamlin ultimately finished sixth at Martinsville, a disappointing result considering what he needed from Sunday's race.

Denny Hamlin Points to Costly First Stage at Martinsville

Hamlin traced his problems back to the opening stage, when his team's strategy left him buried in traffic.

"Really came down to Stage 1," Hamlin said. "Lost all of our track position there."

The setback proved difficult to overcome.

"The first stage was the killer for us that set us back," he explained. "At the end of the first stage, we had to restart last, we had to wave around."

Things only became more complicated once Hamlin found himself racing deeper in the field.

"Then when we got to the back, cautions, the 22 got the 20, then the 20 got into us, but that's racing, I guess," he said.

The contact left Hamlin's No. 11 Toyota with damage, adding another obstacle to an afternoon already heading in the wrong direction.

"We just lost our track position," Hamlin said. "And once we lost our track position, it's just hard to drive back to the front."

At Martinsville, where clean air and track position can be especially valuable, the consequences were substantial. Hamlin had the speed and experience to expect a competitive afternoon, but the race never developed the way his team needed.

Hamlin Still Has One More Goal Before the Season Ends

With only the season finale at Homestead-Miami Speedway remaining, Hamlin's attention is turning toward a different objective.

He still believes he can compete for victories, and he isn't hiding his disappointment that Martinsville wasn't one of them.

"I feel confident I'll be able to contend," Hamlin said. "I'd love to get another win before the end of the year. I thought it was gonna come today."

That last sentence said plenty about his expectations entering Sunday.

Martinsville was supposed to be the place where Hamlin could make one final push toward the championship . Instead, he'll head to Homestead looking to salvage something from a season that once offered considerably bigger possibilities.

"We'll have to get one more shot at it next week," Hamlin said. "One more win."

articles.title: Ernie Sims named FSU's interim defensive coordinator
articles.summary: FSU football has named Ernie Sims the interim defensive coordinator, promoting Greg Moss to safeties coach.
articles.body:
The FSU Seminoles have officially announced the firings of defensive coordinator Tony White and safeties coach Evan Cooper.

They also revealed who will be taking on the roles of all three. Linebackers coach Ernie Sims has been elevated to interim defensive coordinator, and assistant defensive backs coach Greg Moss will coach safeties. Offensive coordinator and wide receivers coach Tim Harris Jr. will now call the plays on offense, which Norvell did for the first eight games.

Sims is in his first season as FSU's linebacker coach after being the assistant linebackers coach in 2025 and a defensive analyst in 2024. The Tallahassee native was an All-American linebacker at FSU in 2004, finishing his three-year career with 200 tackles, 21.0 tackles for loss, 7.0 sacks, three forced fumbles, two interceptions, one fumble recovery, and one blocked kick.

He started his coaching career in 2018 as a strength & conditioning coordinator at FAU before becoming their director of operations in 2019. He was an analyst for USF in 2020 before becoming their linebackers coach in 2021 and 2022. He spent the 2023 season as the linebackers coach at UCF before joining FSU.

Moss is in his fifth season on FSU's coaching staff, having been hired as a defensive analyst in February of 2022. He was named a senior analyst in 2023 and assistant defensive backs coach in 2025.

Harris was hired as FSU's wide receivers coach in 2025 and named the offensive coordinator in 2026 after Gus Malzahn retired. He was UCF's co-offensive coordinator from 2021-22 and offensive coordinator in 2024.

articles.title: Juventus 2 – Napoli 0: Initial reaction and random observations
articles.summary: Thanks to two incredibly pretty second-half goals, Juventus got back to their winning ways with a win over the Partenopei.
articles.body:
As you could probably understand, I was rather worried about how the final hours of Juventus' 129th birthday might actually go. Not because of who they were playing, but mostly because of what they did the last time they took the field. They looked like a team that was on the cusp of even more badness — which, in all fairness, could still be the case a month or two from now.

But on this night, Juventus showed they still have some fight in them.

You combine that fight and mindset with two absolute beauties of goals from Kerim Alajbegović and Jérémie Boga, Juventus actually showed that they can function as an actual team compared to the performance from midweek in Genoa. The 2-0 win on Sunday night over Napoli and old friend (yet suspended) Max Allegri does not fix the problems that we've seen for much of this season, but considering this team spent the last couple of days in ritiro, was called out in a team meeting by their still-new CEO and had a certain section of the fan base protesting their recent efforts in the couple of hours leading up to kickoff.

Just when you were waiting for somebody in that black and white home kit to do something on a night when Juveentus' two strikers struggled mightily to do much of anything in front of goal, leave it to a young man who turned 19 years old all of six weeks ago to deliver this kind of goal when his team desperately needed it.

Just look at that strike. For as good as Boga's goal was to seal the win, the way Alajbegović struck that ball and sent it to a place where Napoli goalkeeper Alex Meret had absolutely no chance was simply lovely. Then you get the kiss off the far post and just realize how much velocity the ball had on it as he bounced across the goal line and into the other side of the net, it's highly unlikely that he could have hit the ball any better than he did.

One win over a Napoli team that has had its own struggles and was without two of its most important pieces, Stanislav Lobotka (injury) and Rasmus Højlund (illness), won't be the thing that suddenly makes us believe that Juventus are a well-oiled machine again. As much as Juventus were the better side for much of Sunday night's game, this was a scoreless affair until the 70th minute. Juve defended well for much of the night, but they also struggled to test Meret for much of this game. Even as they saw Napoli have much of the possession for large portions of the game, Juve were the team who were getting into the box more, causing more trouble for the opposing defense but not actually testing the opposing goalkeeper.

Before Alajbegović's goal, Juve had all of two shots on targets — and it's not like either of them were all that difficult for Meret to collect.

Then came the big right hook after Alajbegović collected a pass from Edon Zhegrova, weaved his way through a couple of Napoli defenders and found a window to shoot. And we sure are glad he did just that.

Because this schedule between the first two international breaks of the season is unrelenting, Juve have all of a few days before they have to try and do it all over again. For all we know, they can revert back to the kind of performance level we saw against Genoa. But if they can, somehow, channel a little bit (or a lot) of what they did against Napoli on Sunday night when they head to the Netherlands then it might be a sign they could get out of this whole mess.

At least for one night we were reminded that this team can actually put out a solid performance when possible.

A red? To a player from the team playing against Juventus? In this economy?

The camera shots to Max in the stands after Juventus went ahead 2-0 were what you expected. That was a man who was none too pleased about what he was seeing from his team.

Napoli didn't score on their first shot on goal. Or, the better phrasing should be that Juventus didn't allow a goal on their first shot on goal against.

It took one heck of a save for that to happen, though. Bravo to you, Vic.

And that turned out to be the only save that Guglielmo Vicario actually had to make on Sunday night. Hey, that sounds like a pretty good reason to say that the defense played well in front of him.

With how good Alajbegović's goal was the shot that Boga took for his will maybe get lost in the shuffle a little bit. But fret not, friendos, that was still a damn good hit and we shall acknowledge him for it!

Easy assist of Andrea Cambiaso's career on Boga's goal? Didn't exactly take a lot of football mastery.

Cambiaso only was able to recorded that assist because one of Sunday's biggest surprises starters, Juan Cabal, had to come off injured. Cabal, for his part, put in the kind of solid performance that has me struggling to remember when he actually played that well. It's been a while, that's the only thing I know for sure. So if Cabal wants to keep that coming, he's more than welcome to because Cambiaso's struggles have left the door wide open for playing time.

Goals from the left wing with shots from outside of the box like Kenan Yildiz likes to do? Not a bad route to follow, I'd say. Keep them coming because we damn well know the strikers ain't scoring much these days.

Speaking of those strikers, Nick Woltemade and Randal Kolo Muani combined to take all of one shot.

That is important because, well, they are strikers. They're not defenders who only come up on corners.

Juventus finished with 18 shots as a team, by the way.

Edon Zhegrova had more shots by himself in a three-minute span than Kolo Muani and Woltemade had in the entire game.

Whole lot of whistles for Kolo Muani as he was subbed off in the second half. Not great, Bob.

Whole lot of whistles when Cambiaso came onto the field, too. That wasn't great, either.

The biggest early sign that this could be a different kind of game than what we saw against Genoa was just that they looked like they were actually up for it. I hate that this has become some sort of requirement that needs to be mentioned any time Juventus don't put forward an absolutely terrible performance, but this is the current state of the club. They showed up on Sunday — and they need to keep that as the norm going forward.

Weston McKennie reportedly came off with an injury at the half. Because that's what this Juve squad needs right now, right? More injuries! Who's excited about that?!?! (Nope, not me. Never, ever me.)

Napoli had four shots in the second half. Two of them came in the final two minutes of stoppage time. That'll do when it comes to a defense playing well.

And a clean sheet … in this economy?!?!?!

This is the first time in a long time I can remember a Napoli game that I've watched in which Scott McTominay has looked as completely ineffective as he did against Juventus on Sunday.

Teun Koopmeiners' defensive effort needs to be recognized because he did a whole lot of it against Napoli.

Watch out because Lorenzo Lucca just tried to flop and get a foul again.

Five key passes for Douglas Luiz. That'll do.

Prayer circle for Kerim that his asking for a sub right after his goal was nothing more than just a minor thing because he is not the kind of player Juve need to see get hurt with all of the other players who are currently out injured. Please be OK, Kerim, because Juventus need you in these next couple of games before the November international break.

Not feeling completely devoid of positive emotions after a Juventus game this season … what is this newfound thing? Can it continue? I am sure happy that Juventus won, played fairly well and didn't do much to piss me off. Hey, sounds like something they should do more often!

Nice way to finish the weekend. Congrats, everybody.

articles.title: Colts coach Shane Steichen plans to 'evaluate everything, every position' after latest loss
articles.summary: (AP) — Indianapolis Colts coach Shane Steichen plans to “evaluate everything, every position.Steichen’s team got steamrolled in Jacksonville, losing 42-7 to...
articles.body:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. (AP) — Indianapolis Colts coach Shane Steichen plans to "evaluate everything, every position."

Steichen's team got steamrolled in Jacksonville, losing 42-7 to the Jaguars five days after trading perennial Pro Bowlers Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner and signaling a potential full-scale rebuild in Indianapolis.

Steichen could be the next one gone. The Colts (2-6) have lost four in a row and 13 of 15 going back to last season. They also lost for the 12th time as the road team against Jacksonville.

"Clearly I got to do a better job, plain and simple," Steichen said. "Starts with me as a head coach. I got to do better job to get these guys ready to go because that wasn't it today."

Indianapolis finished with 243 yards a week after totaling 218 in a loss at Minnesota. It was the fourth time this season the Colts have managed fewer than 260 yards of offense.

"Bottom line is guys got to step up," Steichen said. "That's what it is. Players, coaches, everyone has to step up. We have a job to do and have to do it as a really high level.

"That's our job as professionals to go do that."

Daniel Jones completed 19 of 28 passes for 144 yards, with a touchdown to Josh Downs and two interceptions. He was sacked three times and benched in the fourth quarter, replaced by Anthony Richardson.

Jonathan Taylor ran eight times for 23 yards against the league's top rushing defense, and that was with a 19-yard gain.

"It's embarrassing. It's a butt whooping," Taylor said. "Went down there and they kicked our teeth in. That was an old-fashioned butt whooping. That's what's going to show up on the film."

Taylor responded "I'm part of this" when asked whether he still wanted to remain in Indy.

"My performance was nowhere near up to par," he said. "It's not like I went for 200 yards and five touchdowns and we still lost. No, I'm part of it. I'm also part of the embarrassing butt whooping today."

Downs, whom Steichen acknowledged has requested a trade, left the locker room by the time it was opened to media. He finished with four receptions for 23 yards and returned a punt for 20 yards.

"He did some good things," Steichen said. "He had a couple catches there. But he continued to be a pro throughout the week and then showed up to play today."

Steichen suggested any potential lineup changes could send a message to a team that looked like it had given up on the season. The Colts trailed 28-0 at halftime — they allowed four plays that gained at least 30 yards, including a 92-yard interception returned for a touchdown — and didn't score until they were down by five touchdowns.

"Like I said, everything will be evaluated after this game for sure moving forward," Steichen said.

And he insisted he's not concerned about his job.

"I'm focused on getting better," he said. "That's what I'm focused on right now. Nothing else."

articles.title: Verstappen jokes with new world champion Antonelli in the cooldown room
articles.summary: Kimi Antonelli became Formula 1 world champion for the first time in his career at the Mexican Grand Prix. After the race, Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton...
articles.body:
Kimi Antonelli became Formula 1 world champion for the first time in his career at the Mexican Grand Prix. After the race, Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton praised him in the cooldown room. Verstappen also joked with both drivers.

It was a wonderful moment. As Verstappen entered the cooldown room, Hamilton could be seen with an arm around 20-year-old Antonelli, giving him a hug. "I'm so happy for you," Hamilton began. "I am hoping next year, we can have some..." Hamilton said before signalling some racing action. "For sure," Antonelli replied.

Antonelli enjoyed the final part of the race in Mexico

Antonelli thought the final part of the race in particular was fantastic. "The end of the race was fun; we were all pushing flat out." Verstappen had meanwhile taken a seat on the sofa. Hamilton then pointed out the downside of clipping the speed. "Yeah, that's true. It really kills the overtaking into Turn 1. But you need it," Verstappen replied.

"The brakes were an issue," Antonelli observed. Verstappen and Hamilton nodded in agreement. As they watched footage of Bottas's crash, all three reacted the same way. "That was scary," Antonelli said.

There was a brief silence, but then Verstappen joked with Antonelli. "You've got some green confetti, ha ha." Antonelli tried to wipe them off and asked if they were gone. "No, you need some water," Verstappen said. The Dutchman wet a small towel and handed it to Antonelli.

Hamilton then remarked that Red Bull had a lot of speed on the straight. "You guys have got too much power on the straight," he said. Verstappen had a quick-witted response. "I needed it with your cornering, ha ha." Antonelli then pointed to the brakes.

"Didn't you have a brake issue problems with the brakes?" the Italian asked. "Yeah, at the beginning," Hamilton said. "We had to do a lot of LICO (lift and coast)," Antonelli replied.

articles.title: 3 things we learned about the Cowboys from the Cardinals game
articles.summary: Three things we learned from Sunday’s game
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys lost a heartbreaker to the Arizona Cardinals. Here is what we learned.

It's possible for the Cowboys defense to start fast but can't finish

Dallas forced a punt and had a goal line stand on the Cardinals first two drives, respectively. On the third drive, Shemar James snagged the first interception of his young career, creating a seven-point opportunity on the Cardinals five-yard line. The offense would go on to score a touchdown on a wild fumble recovery by newly elevated James Mitchell.

Tyler Allgeier, however, decided it was time to explode in the third quarter after the quarterback switch to Gardner Minshew. It was exceptionally confusing considering the state of the Cardinals offense. Jeremiyah Love was out, the offense just switched to the backup quarterback. Injuries were ravaging the Cardinals.

But once Arizona finally put up a touchdown, they were not stopped again until the first drive in overtime. It was certainly a disappointing finish on the day for a defense that started out strong as strong as they did. They just can't put a complete game together.

Brian Schottenheimer and the offense once again kept the ball on the ground at a high rate for the second straight week. The offense left some points on the board, and the run game wasn't explosive, but the balance allowed them to be efficient enough through most of the day, putting up 30 total points.

That should have been enough. Somehow, it wasn't.

When the defense allowed Allgeier to break off a massive touchdown run in the third quarter, the Cowboys didn't panic. They continued to run the ball and pass the ball at nearly a 50/50 ratio on the following touchdown drive. When the defense again gave up a touchdown on the next drive, the Cowboys offense immediately stepped in and chewed up nearly seven minutes, finishing with a field goal and going up by two scores.

They ran the ball nine times on that drive. That's the kind of offense you can run to shut out games on any normal week. Unfortunately, as we know, games against the Cardinals are far from normal. It's hard to quantify just how Dallas lost this game.

This two decade long Cardinals nightmare continued the day after Halloween. It looked like Dallas was going to run away with this one, going up 24-10 in the fourth quarter. Then again at 27-17 and just 3:54 to go in the fourth, the game should have been locked up. But the Dallas defense rolled over and allowed the Cardinals to score four back-to-back touchdowns in the second half, tying the game at 30-30 (thanks to a missed Arizona extra point).

And then in overtime, after forcing an Arizona three-and-out, the Cowboys offense had one last shot to go put the game away. They returned the favor by going three-and-out themselves. The defense completely fell apart again on the ensuing drive, allowing a game-winning field goal to the Cardinals.

This was a game that Arizona had no business winning. Yet, as we know, this 2026 Cowboys team just isn't good enough to trust in any game situation. And with that loss, the Cardinals curse continues.

articles.title: 'We've got big problems' - Hamilton says Ferrari need 'serious talks'
articles.summary: Lewis Hamilton says Ferrari need "some serious talks behind closed doors" after fighting between their two drivers in Mexico.
articles.body:
Lewis Hamilton says Ferrari "have to have some serious talks behind closed doors" after fighting between their two drivers cost them victory in the Mexico City Grand Prix.

Leclerc cut a chicane on the first lap to take the lead from Hamilton, who then lost second place to Max Verstappen as a consequence of his team-mate's attack.

Verstappen went on to win the race with Hamilton second as Kimi Antonelli finished third to become the youngest world champion in Formula 1 history.

"Ultimately, that lost us the win today," said Hamilton. "We have to have some serious talks behind closed doors."

During a red-flag period in the race caused by a crash for Valtteri Bottas' Cadillac, Hamilton had said over team radio: "We've got big problems. Big, big problems."

When informed Hamilton was unhappy, Leclerc said: "I will speak with Lewis. We both didn't make the corner. I don't know if Lewis' point was for me to get P3 but having the Red Bull second I felt it was worth it to keep the position and see what happened. That's what I did.

"I could be also unhappy with how much he pushed me off track out of Turn One, but it is racing. When you are fighting for a win it is the way it should be."

Hamilton's point is that if the Ferraris had worked together on the first lap, they would have been running one-two and could have controlled the race from there and likely finished in those positions.

The incident was the latest and arguably most serious of a series of tensions between Hamilton and Leclerc this season.

It follows Leclerc pushing Hamilton off track at the first corner of the Italian Grand Prix.

The race before that, Leclerc ignored a team order to let Hamilton by when they were on different strategies.

In Singapore last month, there was another incident when Hamilton felt he should have been let by when they were on different tyres, but Ferrari refused to make the call.

Verstappen, who capitalised on this latest battle in Mexico, said: "Ferrari were really fast, I do think they made it a little bit difficult for themselves fighting each other and that's why I was able to capitalise on that. I mean, I take it, right?

articles.title: KIMI ANTONELLI MAKES FORMULA 1 HISTORY — THE 20-YEAR-OLD IS OFFICIALLY WORLD CHAMPION!
articles.summary: Formula 1 has a new world champion, and the sport just witnessed history. Kimi Antonelli has officially been crowned the 2026 Formula 1 World Champion, beco...
articles.body:
Formula 1 has a new world champion, and the sport just witnessed history.

Kimi Antonelli has officially been crowned the 2026 Formula 1 World Champion , becoming the youngest driver ever to win the championship after finishing third at the Mexican Grand Prix.

At just 20 years old, the Mercedes superstar has accomplished something that seemed almost impossible when he first arrived in Formula 1.

Antonelli entered the weekend knowing he was on the verge of securing the title. With a massive points advantage over his closest challengers, George Russell and Lewis Hamilton, he only needed a ninth-place finish to guarantee the championship regardless of what his rivals accomplished.

Starting fourth, Antonelli kept his composure through a chaotic race that featured a red flag following Valtteri Bottas' heavy crash and a late safety car. He eventually crossed the line in third place, officially sealing his first career world championship.

Max Verstappen took the race victory, with Hamilton finishing second, but the biggest celebration belonged to Antonelli and Mercedes.

The achievement is even more impressive when looking at the history he just made. Antonelli has broken Sebastian Vettel's record as the youngest Formula 1 world champion, taking the crown at just 20 years and 68 days old.

He also becomes Italy's first F1 world champion since Alberto Ascari in 1953.

This championship is the result of an incredible second season for the young Italian. After facing plenty of pressure and questions during his rookie campaign, Antonelli has responded with a season that has established him as one of the biggest stars in motorsport.

He entered the Mexican Grand Prix with nine victories already under his belt, and now he can add the biggest achievement in racing to his résumé.

Mercedes also returns to the top of the Drivers' Championship for the first time since Lewis Hamilton won the title in 2020.

The future of Formula 1 suddenly looks very different. Antonelli has arrived, and he has already taken the biggest prize the sport has to offer.

At just 20 years old, Kimi Antonelli is a Formula 1 world champion. And if this season is any indication, this could be the beginning of something special.

articles.title: Bulldogs overwhelm Marshfield, take on Bolivar Friday
articles.summary: CARL JUNCTION, Mo. — Carl Junction won its first round of football districts 49-14 against Marshfield Friday and advances to play Bolivar at home in the dist...
articles.body:
CARL JUNCTION, Mo. — Carl Junction won its first round of football districts 49-14 against Marshfield Friday and advances to play Bolivar at home in the district semifinals at 7 p.m. next Friday.

Carl Junction quarterback Burke Diskin had three rushing touchdowns and two passing touchdowns on the night.

"It feels real great, we're keeping the season alive," Diskin said.

Marshfield received the first kick and got things moving on its 33. Carl Junction's defense didn't give much and forced Marshfield to an early 4th and 1. The Blue Jays looked to set the tone early and then converted with a run up the middle. The Bulldogs didn't fold and some strong pass defense forced a 4th and 3 on the CJ 35. Three yards proved too much and it was Bulldog ball.

The Bulldogs' offense started with a quarterback keeper to Diskin, which gained a few yards. Tadem Jones made a run across the midfield before Tristen Lopez took an outside run to the 17. Diskin finished off the drive by following a Lopez block into the end zone. The extra point made it a 7-0 ballgame.

The next drive saw little success for Marshfield. They gained about 15 yards before the ball came loose in a crowd and it wound up in Izic Boles' hands for the Bulldogs.

Two plays is all CJ needed starting on the Marshfield 31. Lopez broke off to gain 5 yards on the ground and Bryant Hanks beat his man on a go route and Diskins put it in his arms. Less than 10 minutes in, CJ led 14-0.

Marshfield faced a 3 and out on its next possession but quarterback and punter Brock Jensen booted it 40 yards and pinned CJ inside its own 10.

A fair catch infraction started Carl on the 5. Lopez broke out for a 9-yard gain and to follow that up Diskin took it the remaining 87 yards on the next play to score his third touchdown of the night.

After the first quarter wrapped up, Marshfield got going. After a few small runs, Jensen hit tight end Boyd Messick for the first down. On the next set of downs, the visitors were in a 3rd and 7 situation. Blayne Fleming batted down a low pass to force a fourth down. Keller Campbell made a play breaking up a pass and getting the turnover on downs.

Nothing came off the turnover and CJ punted. On the first play of the drive Kage Stewart got into the backfield and forced a fumble that he also recovered.

On the Marshfield 19, Lopez took two plays to punch the ball in and set the score at 28-0.

Marshfield got a drive going through the air and a pass interference call sent them to the 15. From there Jensen hit Boyd in the end zone.

Carl responded to the 28-7 score by driving down the field and scoring a touchdown. The touchdown play was a Diskin pass to Maddox Shorter.

Shorter described the play as, "Diskin read the corner, who had moved to cover (Hanks) and found me open." Diskin said, "(That) was not the intent of the play (the intended pass was to Hanks) but the corner moved to cover (Hanks) and (Shorter) was wide open."

Diskin then punched in a 2 point conversion and set the score at 36-7 at the end of the half.

In the third quarter, CJ started with the ball and the drive resulted in another Diskin rushing touchdown. The resulting kickoff saw a fumble recovered by CJ and Diskin scored another rushing touchdown but the extra point was blocked.

Before the end of the third, Marshfield's Anthony Macrelli scored a rushing touchdown.

The fourth quarter saw both teams kill the clock and the game ended 49-14 in favor of CJ.

Bolivar won 42-20 over McDonald County Friday night.

Shorter said, "I think we'll be fine. Our coaches will prep us well all week."
authors: Austin Dye, The Joplin Globe, Mo.

articles.title: NHL Trade Grades for Shane Wright-Matthew Wood Deal Between Kraken and Predators
articles.summary: Shane Wright's name has been on the NHL trade block for more than a year now, especially after he requested a trade out of Seattle early this past offseason.
articles.body:
Shane Wright's name has been on the NHL trade block for more than a year now, especially after he requested a trade out of Seattle early this past offseason.

The Kraken traded Wright, the No. 4 overall pick in the 2022 NHL Draft, to the Nashville Predators in a one-for-one trade that sends forward Matthew Wood the other way.

For Wright, it ends a mostly disappointing five-year run with the Kraken, where he never reached his full potential. Wright entered that 2022 draft as a contender for the No. 1 overall pick, but slid down the board behind Juraj Slafkovsky (No. 1 to the Montreal Canadiens), Simon Nemec (No. 2 to the New Jersey Devils) and Logan Cooley (No. 3 to the then-Arizona Coyotes).

After falling down to the No. 4 overall pick, Wright said he was going to use that as extra motivation and play with a chip on his shoulder.

Outside of a few brief glimpses here and there, it has not quite played out as Wright and the Kraken had hoped.

Now that the trade is complete, let's take a look at some grades for each team.

Trading a player like Wright is never easy.

You recognize the fact that he is still only 22 years old and has shown some ability to be an NHL player. There is still some potential there; there is still plenty of ability, and there is still a chance he puts it all together. If that is going to happen, you want it to happen for your team and not somebody else. That makes you want to keep giving that player an extended look, a long leash, and every opportunity to succeed.

At some point, however, you just have to recognize that, for one reason or another, it is just not working as you hoped. At that point you have to wonder how long you are going to keep waiting for the player to pan out, especially when the player in question has already requested a fresh start.

There are always going to be teams interested in taking a gamble on a player like Wright, but nobody is going to give up a lot for a player that has become more of a suspect than a prospect.

If you are Seattle, you are either going to get a player just like the one you are trading away (a talented, but unproven player that might need a change of scenery), or a mid-round draft pick (or some comparable value to that).

Everybody is just rolling the dice at that point and hoping for lightning in a bottle.

Seattle ended up getting a similar player in Wood.

He is a year younger than Wright, has accomplished a little less in the NHL, and is also probably in need of a fresh start. He is also a different type of player than Wright in terms of style, playing a bigger, more physical, offensive-minded game.

The frustration for Seattle is that, with its first two first-round picks in franchise history, both of which came in the top four(2021 No. 2 overall pick Matty Beniers), they did not get a single impact player out of it. Beniers is good, but he has not taken a big step. Wright has shown flashes, but not consistently. Now he is gone, and now it all shifts to their ability to help Wood reach his potential.

Talent for talent, it is fair value. But it is still a disappointing end to the situation.

Everything that was just said about Seattle and Wright kind of applies to Nashville and Wood.

Inconsistent results and still largely unproven.

You want to see them pan out for you and not somebody else.

Eventually everybody needs a change of scenery, but the trade value is tough.

Even their production has been similar, especially on a per-minute basis.

Since the start of the 2024-25 season, Wright has scored 0.71 goals per 60 minutes of 5-on-5 play, recorded 1.63 total points per 60 minutes and generated 0.71 individual expected goals per 60 minutes.

Wood has averaged 0.75 goals, 1.44 total points, and 0.70 individual expected goals per 60 minutes at 5-on-5.

The only thing that might give Wright a little bit more of an edge is that he might be a better center (which gives some positional value) and a better defensive player, and even with his down year in 2025-26, he did have a 2024-25 season in Seattle that was legitimately pretty good, and the best individual season that either player has had in their limited NHL work.

You can make an argument, based on that, that he is the more accomplished NHL player at this stage of their careers, while also still having the shine of being a recent top-five pick and the upside that could come with it.

It is a solid gamble for Nashville. Now they just have to see if they can help him reach his full potential.

articles.title: Report: Tyler Huntley to have MRI on injured toe
articles.summary: The Ravens had a rough go of it at quarterback on Sunday and it could leave them short on options for Thursday night's game against the Jaguars.
articles.body:
The Ravens had a rough go of it at quarterback on Sunday and it could leave them short on options for Thursday night's game against the Jaguars.

Lamar Jackson was knocked out with a right thumb injury early in the game and head coach Jesse Minter said he could miss the rest of the season after having surgery. Tyler Huntley replaced him, but also had to leave after suffering a toe injury.

Adam Schefter of ESPN reports that Huntley is believed to have turf toe and will have an MRI to determine the extent of the injury. That would also fill in information about the extent of his absence from the lineup, but the quick turnaround to Thursday seems like too much to ask given Huntley's inability to return to Sunday's loss to the Bills.

Rookie Joe Fagnano was the emergency quarterback on Sunday and went 10-of-21 for 91 yards and an interception after the two injuries. The Ravens do not have a quarterback on the practice squad, so they'll need to do something to give themselves more than one healthy player at the position against Jacksonville.

articles.title: Syracuse football: Orange open as slim underdogs to Clemson
articles.summary: All of a sudden, Syracuse is trending upward
articles.body:
The Syracuse Orange have suddenly improved in their opening odds after a two-game winning streak. Syracuse hosts the Clemson Tigers in the JMA Wireless Dome this Saturday. The Orange only opened as +3.5 point underdogs according to FanDuel's opening odds . The odds have since decreased as the Orange are only +1.5 point underdogs as of Sunday evening.

The Orange are coming off a dramatic win over SMU at home this past Saturday. The Mustangs, then ranked No. 19 at the time, came back from down 10 points at half time to take their first lead of the game with nine minutes left in the game. The Orange kicked a field goal then marched 68 yards down the field on 11 plays in 3:19 to retake the lead with 17 seconds left. The Noah Meyers touchdown was just enough for the Orange to hold on for the upset victory.

Steve Angeli threw for 200 yards and the game-winning touchdown on 21-24 passing with no interceptions. He also added a 26-yard rushing touchdown. The Orange defense just barely survived, despite SMU quarterback Kevin Jennings throwing for 352 yards and two touchdowns.

The victory gives Syracuse two ACC wins on the season. The Orange had lost its previous 11 ACC games prior to last week. The win also moves Syracuse to a 4-4 record, needing just two wins for bowl eligibility.

Clemson got back into the win column with a victory at Florida State. The Tigers scored over 30 points for the first time in ACC play this season as Clemson took down the Seminoles 36-24. The game would be the last that Mike Norvell coached as the leader of Florida State, as he was fired on Sunday afternoon.

The Tigers enter the JMA Wireless Dome at 5-3 on the season. Clemson lost at LSU to open the year and also got blown out by Miami. The Tigers also lost to James Franklin's Virginia Tech team in Death Valley.

Syracuse won for the third time in history against Clemson last season. Angeli threw for 245 yards and two touchdowns in the game before tearing his Achilles. Justus Ross-Simmons had two touchdown catches and Johntay Cook had 113 receiving yards as the Orange won 34-21 over the Tigers in Death Valley.

Kickoff for Saturday's marquee matchup is set for 12:00 pm ET. The game will air on ESPN2.

articles.title: Vikings defense holds Lions in check for 3 quarters before buckling late
articles.summary: DETROIT (AP) — For the first six games of the season, the Minnesota Vikings were able to count on their top-tier defense to bail out an inconsistent offense....
articles.body:
DETROIT (AP) — For the first six games of the season, the Minnesota Vikings were able to count on their top-tier defense to bail out an inconsistent offense.

As a result, the Vikings went into Detroit on Sunday at 6-0 — the last undefeated team in the NFL. The Vikings were allowing a league-best 12.3 points per game, and were in the top 10 in points allowed, rushing yards allowed and passing yards allowed.

For 30 minutes, none of that changed. The Lions only had 154 yards and six points in the first half, while Minnesota had sacked Jared Goff four times and became the first team this season to intercept him.

"We have total trust and confidence in our defense," Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell said. "We know they are capable of keeping us in every game."

That defense, though, struggled a bit in the second half. Jahmyr Gibbs rushed for 116 of his 153 yards and a touchdown, and little-used No. 2 running back Sione Vaki carried six times for 36 yards.

"If you cannot run it on these guys, you're going to struggle and we got it going, particularly in the second half," coach Dan Campbell said.

Even wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown picked up a first down on a play where he lined up wide, 10 yards behind the line of scrimmage, then caught a screen pass that counted as a lateral.

"What they do is kind of wacky so you have to be wacky and fight fire with fire," Goff said, adding the team had worked on the play for just a few days.

Early in the fourth quarter, with the Lions leading 12-7, the defense forced a three-and-out with 12:48 left. Jack Fox's punt was caught at the Vikings 16, but Minnesota went 84 yards in seven plays for Kyler Murray's touchdown pass to T.J. Hockenson with 8:44 to play.

The 2-point conversion was successful, giving the Vikings a 15-12 lead, but that's when the Lions took over. Gibbs carried the ball three times for 35 yards and Vioki had two carries for 22 yards and a reception for 5.

That moved Detroit to the Vikings 7, where Jared Goff hit Jameson Williams for a touchdown and a 19-15 lead.

The Minnesota offense only gained 5 yards in three plays, giving them a fourth-and-5 from their 33 with 3:01 to play.

O'Connell's faith in his defense never wavered. He decided to punt.

"We had all three timeouts left, plus the two-minute warning," he said. "There was an opportunity for the defense to get a stop and get us the ball back."

Gibbs, though, ran for 22 yards on the first two plays of the drive, taking the clock down to two minutes, and the Lions picked up two more first downs before moving into the victory formation.

The Vikings held the league's second-best scoring offense to 19 points, 11.6 below their season average. That's an outstanding performance — it just wasn't good enough to save a staggering offense.

"It's November, and we're still looking for that complete 60-minute game," O'Connell said. "We need to start playing with the right amount of urgency."

articles.title: Mike Vrabel’s Challenge Aided Drake Maye’s Long Touchdown To Kyle Williams
articles.summary: A replay review changed the call in the end-zone and gave New England a much-needed spark.
articles.body:
The Patriots needed something to change against the Dolphins. Mike Vrabel gave them a chance to make it happen when he sent the officials back to review a key call.

The challenge went New England's way. The Patriots needed it: Drake Maye found Kyle Williams for a 43-yard touchdown that brought the Patriots back into the game.

The touchdown was the kind of explosive play New England had been missing. The Patriots had struggled to turn promising possessions into points, including a missed field goal earlier in the game. This time, Vrabel's decision helped preserve the chance to finish the drive, and Maye delivered with a deep strike to Williams.

The Patriots' official accoun t captured both sides of the sequence: Vrabel launching the challenge flag.

Also, Williams celebrating the touchdown. The timing made the scoring play feel even bigger.

New England had been trailing 13-3, and the 43-yard connection cut Miami's lead to 13-10.

Maye and Williams gave the Patriots the finish they needed, but Vrabel's challenge was the turning point that gave them the opening. A successful review does not guarantee points. This one gave New England a chance, and the quarterback and rookie receiver made the most of it.

articles.title: Antonelli heads list of F1's youngest champions
articles.summary: As Kimi Antonelli becomes F1's youngest world champion, we look at how his achievement compares with some of the drivers who previously held the record.
articles.body:
Kimi Antonelli has made history by becoming the youngest title winner in the 77th year of the Formula 1 World Championship.

The Italian, at 20 years and 68 days, has beaten the record of Sebastian Vettel, who was 23 years and 133 days old when he won the first of his four drivers' championships in 2010.

Antonelli, who was still a teenager until 25 August, has secured the title in his second season in the sport.

We take a look at F1's other young champions and how Antonelli's achievement compares with theirs.

Stage of his F1 career when title was won: Second full season

F1 debut: 2025 Australian Grand Prix (aged 18)

Antonelli has already broken a number of records on the way to becoming F1's youngest champion.

In his second season, he became the youngest driver to achieve a pole position in China and the youngest to lead the championship at the next race in Japan.

In Monaco, he became the youngest driver to complete a 'grand slam' of pole position, fastest lap, leading every lap and winning the race.

All this after a rookie season in 2025 in which there were occasional highs but plenty of errors, and his final total of 150 points was less than half of the 319 accumulated by Mercedes team-mate George Russell.

Stage of his F1 career when title was won: Third full season

Vettel was one of four drivers who could win the title going into the season-ending 2010 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix.

He was far from the best placed, though, trailing Ferrari's Fernando Alonso by 15 points before the race and his Red Bull team-mate Mark Webber by seven.

The German did what he had to do by winning the grand prix and Alonso could only finish seventh, having become stuck behind the Renault of Vitaly Petrov.

With Webber in eighth, Vettel won the championship by four points from Alonso.

It was yet another F1 record for Vettel. He had become the youngest F1 points scorer on his debut for BMW Sauber in Indianapolis in 2007, before becoming the then youngest pole sitter and race winner at the 2008 Italian Grand Prix for Toro Rosso.

F1 debut: 2007 Australian Grand Prix (aged 22)

Lewis Hamilton's debut season in 2007 almost delivered a fairytale title but he faltered in the final two races of the year.

He failed to score in China and finished seventh in Brazil, which allowed Ferrari's Kimi Raikkonen to pip both Hamilton and fellow McLaren driver Fernando Alonso by a single point.

Somehow the climax to the 2008 championship, also in Brazil, was even more dramatic.

Hamilton was battling for the title with Ferrari's home favourite Felipe Massa and the Briton's fourth place was going to be enough to secure the crown when a late rain shower changed everything.

Leader Massa and Hamilton were among those who changed to intermediate tyres but Toyota's Timo Glock stayed out, which lifted him up to fourth.

Hamilton, now in fifth, had Toro Rosso's Vettel right behind him and couldn't afford to lose another position. With just over two laps to go, he ran wide and Vettel was through.

Massa crossed the line to win the race with Hamilton still sixth. The Ferrari pit crew, Massa's family and the Brazilian fans celebrated but with the rain intensifying, Glock was slowing on his dry-weather tyres and Hamilton passed him into the final corner to take the title by a single point. It was heart-stopping stuff.

Stage of his F1 career when title was won: Fourth full season

F1 debut: 2001 Australian Grand Prix (aged 19)

Alonso established control of the 2005 championship early in the season by winning four of the first seven races and never relinquished it.

The Spaniard's speed and consistency ensured he prevailed over Raikkonen, whose McLaren-Mercedes was fast but fragile. A third place at the Brazilian Grand Prix was enough to give Alonso the title with two races to spare.

He won a second consecutive title in 2006, also for Renault, and the 45-year-old remains one of the great personalities and outstanding talents in F1.

He'll be back for another season with Aston Martin in 2027, 26 years after his debut for Minardi.

Stage of his F1 career when title was won: Seventh full season

F1 debut: 2015 Australian Grand Prix (aged 17)

Hamilton won the title on the final lap of the 2008 season but he would lose it on the final lap in 2021 in circumstances that remain a source of huge controversy.

His rival in a thrilling and intense season-long duel was Red Bull's Max Verstappen. There were plenty of flashpoints along the way and it all came to a climax in Abu Dhabi.

Verstappen and Hamilton went into the final race of the season level on points. The Dutchman qualified on pole but Mercedes' Hamilton beat him off the line and largely controlled the race thereafter, until Williams' Nicholas Latifi crashed with five laps to go, bringing out a safety car.

Hamilton did not have enough of an advantage over second-placed Verstappen to pit for fresh tyres and maintain the lead, so stayed out. Verstappen, with nothing to lose, came in and fitted softs.

Race director Michael Masi allowed the lapped cars between Hamilton and Verstappen to go past, but not those behind the Red Bull. He allowed the race to restart for one final racing lap and Verstappen overtook Hamilton, who was a sitting duck on his old hard tyres.

Verstappen and Hamilton, in their own ways, were both stunned and Mercedes team boss Toto Wolff shouted over the radio to Masi: "No, Michael, no! That was so not right!"

As happened with Vettel from 2010-13, this was the first of four consecutive titles for a Red Bull driver with Verstappen dominating the 2022, 2023 and 2024 seasons.

F1 debut: 1970 British Grand Prix (aged 23)

Emerson Fittipaldi became the first Brazilian driver to win the F1 world title in 1972, with five wins from 12 races enough for the Lotus driver to get the better of Jackie Stewart.

Fittipaldi would secure another drivers' title for McLaren two years later but his race-winning days, in F1 at least, were over once he joined his brother's Fittipaldi team in 1976. He would have late-career success in IndyCars, winning the 1989 title and the Indy 500 twice, in 1989 and 1993.

He remained F1's youngest champion for 33 years until Alonso's first title ushered in an era where the record would change hands more regularly.

articles.title: Patriots vs. Dolphins live updates: Score, news, discussion for NFL Week 8
articles.summary: The Patriots have traveled to Miami for their third AFC East matchup of the season.
articles.body:
Despite coming out of a mini-bye, the New England Patriots are battered and bruised heading into their Week 8 contest with the Miami Dolphins. And yet, the team of head coach Mike Vrabel has a real chance to come away as winners: at 4-3, it has performed significantly better thus far this year than its 1-5 opponent.

While season-long records mean little come kickoff, the Patriots are still the more talented team overall even with several starters missing the game on the offensive side of the ball. Nonetheless, as long as Drake Maye remains under center, the team should be able to put pressure on its opponent and compete for a chance to retain a spotless record against the AFC East this year: New England won its first two division games, and is now looking to improve to 3-0.

Will the team be able to do so on the road? Let's find out together. Welcome to our Patriots-Dolphins live tracker and community discussion.

Sunday, Nov. 1, 4:25 p.m. ET | Hard Rock Stadium (Miami Gardens, FL) | Broadcast information | Game day roster | Inactives | Weather forecast

Despite winning the coin toss, the Dolphins decided to start the game on offense. The plan did not work out: New England forced a quick three-and-out, with Marcus Jones running the ensuing punt back 26 yards to give his offense possession at its own 49.

New England's offense started in good field position, and did manage to take advantage. Following three straight runs, Drake Maye hit Hunter Henry for a 20-yard gain to bring his team on the cusp of the red zone. However, once inside the Miami 20, the series stalled out. Andy Borregales ended it by splitting the uprights from 34 yards out. | Patriots 3 : 0 Dolphins

Miami started its next possession with a big return of its own, taking the kickoff after Borregales' field goal all the way out to the 47-yard line. However, Cory Durden's second sack in two drives plus Christian Barmore blowing up a third down on another quarterback takedown forced a second straight quick punt.

The Patriots' next drive was a rough one. First, a Tanner Arkin holding penalty backed the team up. Then, two plays later, Efton Chism lost a fumble while trying to gain extra yards after a short reception. The turnover set up the Dolphins with a first down at the New England 19-yard line.

Luckily for their offense, the Patriots defense continued to play excellent football on the next series to force a quick stop. Cory Durden, who was involved in sacks on each of the first two drives, disrupted another play on second down to eventually help hold Miami to a 31-yard field goal. | Patriots 3 : 3 Dolphins

Corey Kiner, who entered the game as RB2 with TreVeyon Henderson out, kickstarted New England's next drive with a 20-yard carry. The big play did move the team into Dolphins territory, but it once again failed to capitalize: the series ended when ex-Patriot Joshua Uche beat left guard Walter Rouse on a stunt to take down Maye for a 10-year loss on 3rd-and-8.

After three straight three-and-outs, running back Ollie Gordon picked up Miami's first first down of the afternoon. He ended the first quarter with another solid run, and Miami at its own 29-yard line.

The Dolphins continued moving the ball well coming out of the quarter break, including on a 23-yard pass to Malik Washington against a zone coverage structure. However, the defense shored up on its side of the field. Cory Durden was involved in another tackle for loss, with Elijah Ponder and Jaylen Reed teaming up on a sack. Their efforts did not prevent Miami from taking its first lead of the day, though, when Zane Gonzalez made a 52-yard field goal. | Patriots 3 : 6 Dolphins

The Patriots' next drive showed some promise early on. The team still had to convert a 4th-and-2 to keep the series alive, but Drake Maye shrugging off a sack attempt and finding Efton Chism downfield helped solve that problem. However, he couldn't get enough on a third-down scramble following a bad snap to move the chains. To make matters worse, Andy Borregales sent his subsequent 40-yard field goal attempt wide to the right to keep the score at 6-3 in Miami's favor.

The Patriots had an opportunity to get the ball back quickly inside the two-minute warning of the first half, but they allowed Miami to convert a 3rd-and-8 while Marcus Jones failed to reel in an interception on the very next play. An unnecessary roughness penalty against Christian Elliss then put the Dolphins squarely into field goal range, with an 18-yard pass giving them 1st-and-goal at the New England 7. Two plays later, the home team was in the end zone for the game's first touchdown. | Patriots 3 : 13 Dolphins

The Patriots modified their offensive line coming out of the half, replacing left guard Walter Rouse with Ben Brown. However, the change up front did not lead to a change of fortunes: New England went three-and-out to open the third quarter, with Drake Maye getting sacked on 3rd-and-6 to end the series.

New England nearly got a big play on its next drive. However, despite betting his hands on the football, Craig Woodson was unable to complete an interception that would have given the Patriots the ball in Miami territory. The pass breakup still forced the offense off the field on a three-and-out, but it felt like a missed opportunity nonetheless.

Rhamondre Stevenson did the heavy lifting early on during the Patriots' next possession, but it was Drake Maye and Kyle Williams who capped it off in style. Yes, it did take a Mike Vrabel challenge flag to overturn a bad incompletion call on the field, but the end result was a touchdown nonetheless: Maye and the second-year wideout connected from 43-yard out to bring New England within three points. | Patriots 10 : 13 Dolphins

Miami started yet another drive with a long kickoff return, setting up shop at its own 35-yard line on its next possession. However, an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty against running back Ollie Gordon forced the team into a 3rd-and-20 situation it was unable to convert. Three-and-out.

The Patriots followed the recipe that worked on the previous drive on their next possession. Rhamondre Stevenson did some hard running to open the drive, with Drake Maye then hitting DeMario Douglas on a 26-yard gain to get New England into field goal range. Once there, the team bypassed a 41-yard field goal attempt to go for it on 4th-and-2. Initially ruled short of the sticks, a review determined that Douglas had indeed crossed the line to keep the drive alive. Six plays later, Maye found the end zone: he faked the pitch on 3rd-and-goal from the 2-yard line to create an opening, capping off a 73-yard scoring drive in style. | Patriots 17 : 13 Dolphins

articles.title: Big 12 Conference admits officials got call wrong that benefited BYU Cougars in win over Arizona State
articles.summary: The Big 12 admitted replay errors in BYU's games against Notre Dame and Arizona State, raising questions about the conference's officiating process.
articles.body: Maybe the BYU Cougars being a religious school can pay some dividends. The Cougars have benefited from a very fortunate run of officiating in recent weeks. At home against the then-No. 2 ranked Notre Dame Fighting Irish, BYU pulled off a stunning upset. Thanks in small part to yet another controversial literal last second clock call this college football season. Quarterback Bear Bachmeier found tight end Walker Lyons with 1:47 remaining in the fourth quarter to give the Cougars a 28-24 lead, putting Notre Dame's winning streak in jeopardy. The Irish drove down the field, converting a six-yard pass on fourth-and-5 to give themselves one last shot at the end zone from the 8-yard line with four seconds left. C.J. Carr's pass fell incomplete, and fans stormed the field. BIG 12 CONFERENCE ADDRESSES OFFENSIVE CHANTS FROM UCF FANS DIRECTED AT BYU DURING UPSET WIN Except, eagle-eyed viewers noticed that the stadium game clock clearly read 0:01 as the ball hit the turf. And the Big 12 Conference acknowledged they were right, and that Notre Dame should have had time for one last play. "Following the Big 12's review of the final play of Saturday's Notre Dame-BYU game, it was determined that time remained on the clock when the ball hit the ground and the play was incorrectly cleared by the replay officiating crew," they explained in a statement. "The Conference will conduct a complete review of its end-of-game officiating process in advance of next week's games." Yes, BYU may still have stopped the Irish and won the game anyway, but it was a clear officiating mistake that benefited the Cougars. It happened again the next week. On the road at UCF, BYU found themselves locked in a tight game late in the fourth quarter against what should have been an overmatched opponent. With the game tied 24-24 and 11 seconds left, the Knights set up for a field goal attempt on third down. Kicker Will Stone's attempted was blocked without crossing the line of scrimmage, and Stone recovered it himself. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER As he was tackled, his helmet came off, with the officials throwing a flag for a BYU facemask. Which they promptly picked up. Not only that, they then incorrectly applied a 10-second runoff for the helmet coming off. As rules analysts explained, that runoff is only required when the helmet coming off is the reason for the clock stoppage. But the clock also stopped because of a "legal kick down," per Terry McAulay, meaning that the runoff should not have been applied. Instead of UCF having another opportunity at a game-winning field goal, the game went to overtime. That said, the Cougars did wind up losing in double overtime anyway, thanks in part to some less-than-beneficial officiating. As Stone made a field goal to go up 34-31, BYU's Kendall Wall was flagged for roughing the kicker. Instead of the Cougars needing just a field goal to tie the score, UCF converted the ensuing first-and-goal for a touchdown, making the two-point conversion as well. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE BYU had four tries from the four-yard-line, but came up empty, and the Knights pulled off the upset. Still, there's a case to be made that the game may never have reached overtime in the first place, had the rules been correctly applied. Well, fast-forward to BYU-Arizona State on Halloween, and it happened again. Though at least this mistake wasn't in the closing seconds of the game. In the first quarter in Provo, Bachmeier tried to run the ball in for a touchdown from the one-yard line, but fumbled immediately after the snap. Sione Moa jumped on it, advancing it into the end zone for a touchdown. Replay review confirmed that Bachmeier had indeed fumbled, and separately confirmed that Moa had scored. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! But the review team should never have allowed the touchdown to stand, because the whistle blew on the play to signal that Bachmeier had been ruled down. Once that happened, the ball could not be advanced after a fumble. Inexplicably though, they awarded the Cougars a TD anyway. And now the Big 12 Conference has been forced to issue yet another statement that the officiating crew had made a mistake. "Replay was incorrect in awarding a score," the statement read. "The correct ruling should have been BYU ball for a third-and-goal from the 2-yard line." Sure, the Cougars may have punched it in from the two, but you never know in college football, and the call handed them a touchdown that should not have happened. Understandably, ASU head coach Kenny Dillingham was furious with the officiating crew at the time, and after the game. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD "I was trying to argue that he does have the right to recover it post-whistle, but that's not a clear advancement, which means the ball should be at the three," he said. "Obviously, that wasn't what happened. It's not the officials' fault. Those officials don't have say in that. That's all back home." There's little doubt that these mistakes are simply that, mistakes, and not some grand conspiracy by the Big 12 Conference to help get BYU to the College Football Playoff. But it's a sign of the seemingly growing officiating problem in college football, and yet another example of the fact that referees can, and often do, impact a game negatively. Some Cougars fans will also be quick to point out any number of calls they believe went against their team. Normally, over the course of a season, these things even out. It's just unfortunate when there are several high-profile mistakes all happening around the same program. BYU has yet another massive game this Saturday, as they travel up the road to play their heated rivals, the Utah Utes, in Salt Lake City. The No. 3 Utah Utes and No. 7 BYU Cougars. Just as everyone expected. And given the tight Big 12 race, with Utah 5-0, BYU 4-1 and Texas Tech 4-1, it could have tremendous implications in determining which teams will play in the conference championship game, as well as a spot in the playoff. Hopefully we're not talking about the refs after this one.
